1	# 0020. Require high-assurance Phase 1 suite qualification
     2	
     3	- **Status:** accepted
     4	- **Date:** 2026-07-20
     5	- **Deciders:** Brian
     6	- **Related:** M17; `docs/execution/phase1-suite-review.md`; v4 Part XXII Phase 1;
     7	  R4 §§2, 8, 10, 11.6; ADR-0005; ADR-0013
     8	
     9	## Context
    10	
    11	M17 already requires a proposed Phase 1 suite, coverage matrices, mutation and
    12	fuzz evidence, and two independent adversarial passes. Those nouns do not set a
    13	qualification bar. A suite can claim each artifact while using trivial mutants,
    14	short fuzz runs, shared oracles, vacuous predicates, or reviews that contaminate
    15	one another.
    16	
    17	Phase 1 will freeze foundations used by later parsers, graph projections,
    18	recovery, revision tracking, and external adapters. Test quantity is therefore
    19	not enough. Ratification needs evidence that the suite detects seeded defects,
    20	survives malformed state, reproduces failures, and has no unexamined critical
    21	requirement. The campaign must remain finite so it can be repeated after fixes.
    22	
    23	## Decision
    24	
    25	Phase 1 suite ratification SHALL use the **HAQP-1 high-assurance qualification
    26	profile** below. Passing HAQP-1 does not ratify the suite; it only makes the
    27	proposed packet eligible for Brian's separate T1 ratification decision.
    28	
    29	### 1. Two execution lanes
    30	
    31	- The **continuous lane** runs deterministic unit, integration, regression,
    32	  malformed-input, and gate-canary tests on ordinary changes. It includes
    33	  `just ci` and must not depend on elapsed-time fuzz success.
    34	- The **qualification lane** runs from one fixed clean commit and source tree.
    35	  It contains every HAQP-1 item and is rerun in full after the last verified
    36	  defect is fixed. Partial reruns are diagnostic evidence only.
    37	- Every command, exact toolchain and dependency version, lockfile hash, target,
    38	  seed, declared non-locked regression/fuzz corpus hash, environment
    39	  classification, exit status, and raw artifact hash is recorded. Missing
    40	  evidence fails closed.
    41	
    42	#### Qualification provenance amendment (2026-08-12)
    43	
    44	The qualification packet is committed after its fixed-base campaign. Its
    45	provenance records the campaign commit and that commit's tree hash. The
    46	qualification commit MUST have exactly that campaign commit as its first
    47	parent; the verifier checks parent and tree hashes, requires a clean tree, and
    48	rejects any other provenance shape. This parent-binding design avoids a
    49	self-referential packet commit hash while keeping evidence tied to one clean
    50	source tree. No external manifest or signing key is required.
    51	
    52	### 2. Bidirectional requirements traceability
    53	
    54	- Every Phase 1 normative law, `MUST`, threat boundary, abuse case, fault class,
    55	  work-order exit criterion, and ratification gate has a stable requirement ID.
    56	- Every ID maps to at least one test, and every test maps back to at least one
    57	  ID. Machine verification rejects duplicates, orphans, unknown IDs, and missing
    58	  critical rows.
    59	- Every applicable law has positive, negative, malformed/adversarial,
    60	  basis/provenance, and deterministic-replay evidence. Stateful laws also have
    61	  injected-fault and idempotent-recovery evidence.
    62	- Uncovered critical rows cannot be waived inside the packet. Any exception is
    63	  an exact coordinate accepted through a separate T1 amendment; wildcards,
    64	  whole-file exclusions, and substring allowances are forbidden.
    65	
    66	### 3. Tests of the tests
    67	
    68	- Qualification predeclares at least **64 semantic mutants** across critical
    69	  surfaces. Operators include predicate deletion/inversion, threshold ±1,
    70	  missing enum or kind dispatch, success/error substitution, stale-Basis
    71	  acceptance, wrong Holder/profile selection, skipped durable transition,
    72	  disabled crash point, ordering nondeterminism, oracle short-circuit, and
    73	  broadened allow-list.
    74	- Every critical surface family receives at least eight mutants, and no single
    75	  operator supplies more than one quarter of the denominator. Mutation selection
    76	  cannot cluster around easy-to-kill utility paths.
    77	- Mutation score is **100% of applicable, non-duplicate, non-equivalent
    78	  mutants**. One survivor blocks eligibility.
    79	- An equivalent or duplicate disposition names the mutant, shows the proof, and
    80	  receives concurring verification in both adversarial-pass records. Disposed
    81	  mutants remain visible in the numerator/denominator report.
    82	- Every ratification gate and every M17 Level-3 measurement conjunct gets at
    83	  least one disposable gate canary: a deliberate violation must make the exact
    84	  expected gate fail. Canary execution occurs outside the working tree and
    85	  restores the fixed review base afterward.
    86	
    87	### 4. Generated, metamorphic, and fuzz evidence
    88	
    89	- Five critical surface families each execute at least **100,000 accepted
    90	  deterministic generated cases** from recorded seeds: source/CST/formatting,
    91	  graph/interchange codecs, transforms/projections, repair/ILRP/recovery, and
    92	  Basis/revision/query invalidation.
    93	- Generator attempts and discards are recorded. Discard rate above one percent,
    94	  post-failure filtering, or shrinking the declared domain fails qualification.
    95	- Each family defines independent metamorphic relations where applicable:
    96	  canonical reparse, idempotent replay, inverse/undo, irrelevant-input
    97	  invariance, commuting independent transactions, incremental/full equivalence,
    98	  and deterministic permutation. A relation is not proved by calling the
    99	  implementation's own equality or normalization path on both sides.
   100	- Each family also receives one **30-minute sanitizer-enabled fuzz campaign**
   101	  with at least 16 predeclared seeds spanning valid, boundary, truncated,
   102	  malformed, and hostile input. Total fuzz budget is at least 150 target-minutes.
   103	- Every crash, panic, timeout, memory error, divergence, or minimized failure is
   104	  a failing result. Minimized artifacts become named regression fixtures before
   105	  the qualification lane is rerun.
   106	- Concurrent code receives deterministic schedule exploration. If Phase 1 adds
   107	  no concurrent implementation, the packet records the condition as not
   108	  applicable rather than fabricating coverage.
   109	
   110	### 5. Oracle and fault independence
   111	
   112	- Incremental and full-reparse oracles may share raw bytes and published data
   113	  schemas only. They may not share parser events, lowering code, canonicalizers,
   114	  anchor recovery, comparison shortcuts, or expected-result construction.
   115	- Expected values come from fixed literals, worked spec examples, or a separately
   116	  implemented oracle. Self-snapshots generated by the system under test are not
   117	  authority without independent verification.
   118	- Every registered durable-transition crash boundary is injected immediately
   119	  before and after the transition. Recovery runs twice and must reach the same
   120	  terminal state without hidden staged data, duplicate effects, or mixed Basis.
   121	- Fault matrix is exhaustive over registered boundaries. Runtime discovery and
   122	  declared inventory must match exactly; either-side drift fails.
   123	
   124	### 6. Independent adversarial review
   125	
   126	- Pass 1 attacks implementation and packet for vacuity, shared-oracle coupling,
   127	  missing negatives, weak mutants, fault omissions, nondeterminism, corpus
   128	  leakage, exception broadening, and evidence/report drift.
   129	- Pass 2 starts from the original spec and fixed review base. It cannot read Pass
   130	  1 prompts, findings, dispositions, or fixes until it records its own findings.
   131	- Passes use distinct reviewer identities and isolated conversation/session
   132	  state. If both reviewers are automated, they use different model families;
   133	  otherwise at least one reviewer is human. Sanitized prompt and reviewer
   134	  identity hashes are recorded without credentials or secret material.
   135	- Each pass records at least 12 concrete falsification attempts, including
   136	  attempted violations that the suite correctly catches. Findings cite exact
   137	  evidence and are independently reproduced before any fix.
   138	- Zero verified findings may remain unresolved. False positives remain recorded
   139	  with reproduction evidence; they are not silently deleted.
   140	
   141	### 7. Bounded campaign and residual risk
   142	
   143	- HAQP-1 qualification is a review-candidate campaign, not a per-edit tax. Its
   144	  intended wall-clock ceiling is eight hours on the recorded reference machine.
   145	  Crossing that ceiling twice blocks ratification and triggers a superseding ADR
   146	  or harness optimization; thresholds cannot be silently reduced.
   147	- Packet lists every known limitation with owner, severity, trigger, affected
   148	  requirement, evidence, and planned resolution phase. "Future work" without
   149	  those coordinates is invalid.
   150	- Locked acceptance corpora remain black-box inputs touched only by existing
   151	  approved verifiers. HAQP-1 does not authorize inspecting, listing, copying,
   152	  hashing, or deriving new fixtures from locked corpus contents.
   153	
   154	**What would falsify or reverse this:** two clean qualification attempts exceed
   155	the eight-hour ceiling, required tooling cannot produce reproducible evidence,
   156	or HAQP-1 encourages equivalent-mutant or low-value-case inflation without
   157	finding real seeded defects. Reversal requires a superseding ADR with measured
   158	campaign data and cannot weaken already-recorded failures or erase artifacts.
   159	
   160	## Consequences
   161	
   162	- **Positive:** ratification evidence demonstrates sensitivity, independence,
   163	  replayability, traceability, and fault coverage instead of test count alone.
   164	- **Negative:** final qualification consumes up to eight hours, requires at
   165	  least 64 reviewed mutants and 150 target-minutes of fuzzing, and makes every
   166	  post-campaign defect fix trigger another full run.
   167	- **Follow-ups:** AM-17.1 binds M17's packet gate and review records to HAQP-1.
   168	  Phase 1 work orders must budget both execution lanes without ratifying the
   169	  suite automatically.
   170	
   171	## Alternatives considered
   172	
   173	- **Coverage percentages plus ordinary CI** — rejected because high line or
   174	  branch coverage does not show that assertions detect semantic defects.
   175	- **Unbounded fuzzing and exhaustive model checking** — rejected because results
   176	  cannot be repeated on a review schedule and termination becomes subjective.
   177	- **Broad source-wide mutation testing** — rejected because utility-code mutants
   178	  inflate cost and score while diluting critical contract coverage.

    12	# R-008 — a file-scoped ruling is RISK-004, disclosed, not a defect
    13	
    14	**DRAFT. Not in force until Brian sets `status: ruled`, fills `ruled_by` and
    15	`date`, and commits it signed against `conformance/haqp/ruling-signers`.**
    16	
    17	**Finding ruled on.** Blind pass 1 at lane base `cbed339f`, attempt A08
    18	(exception broadening): "Branch at crates/liminal-xtask/src/haq.rs:3166 accepts
    19	whole-file target plus substring phrase matches, bypassing required
    20	exact-coordinate exception scope."
    21	
    22	**What is true.** A ruling whose `target` names a file, not a coordinate, clears
    23	a matching claim anywhere in that file, and the claim is matched by required
    24	and excluded phrases. That is RISK-004 verbatim: "a standing ruling can clear a
    25	finding it does not answer: whether two sentences describe one claim is not
    26	decidable from the sentences." AM-17.15 keeps RISK-004 recorded, because it is
    27	the qualifier reasoning about its own findings.
    28	
    29	**Why file scope is intended.** R-001..R-006 rule on classes of claim that
    30	recur anywhere in `haq.rs` (stage reads of the corpus, a gate not catching its
    31	own change), and a coordinate goes stale with every edit to the file. The
    32	existing mitigations stay: a coordinate-scoped ruling is held to its
    33	coordinate, a ruling clears at most one attempt per record, and excluded
    34	phrases carve out neighbouring claims. Requiring coordinates for every ruling
    35	would retire R-001..R-006 and force each to be re-signed at a coordinate that
    36	moves.
    37	
    38	**Effect.** A verified finding of class `exception broadening` on
    39	`crates/liminal-xtask/src/haq.rs` whose claim is that a ruling's file-scoped
    40	target and phrase matching clear claims outside its intended scope is cleared
    41	while this ruling is `ruled`. It does not clear a claim about signatures,
    42	signers, drafts or status. Those are the controls that keep a ruling Brian's,
    43	and are excluded by name.

    24	/// Lossless coarse CST document. `source` is authoritative for emit, so even
    25	/// malformed or unsupported syntax survives byte-for-byte.
    26	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    27	pub struct CstDocument {
    28	    /// Original UTF-8 source bytes.
    29	    pub source: String,
    30	    /// Coarse blocks discovered without rejecting input.
    31	    pub blocks: Vec<OpaqueBlock>,
    32	}
    33	
    34	/// Parse source without rejection or panics.
    35	#[must_use]
    36	pub fn coarse_parse(source: &str) -> CstDocument {
    37	    let mut blocks = Vec::new();
    38	    let mut block_start = 0usize;
    39	    let mut cursor = 0usize;
    40	    let mut in_block = false;
    41	    for line in source.split_inclusive('\n') {
    42	        let content = line.strip_suffix('\n').unwrap_or(line);
    43	        let blank = content.trim().is_empty();
    44	        if blank {
    45	            if in_block {
    46	                blocks.push(block(source, block_start, cursor));
    47	                in_block = false;
    48	            }
    49	        } else if !in_block {
    50	            block_start = cursor;
    51	            in_block = true;
    52	        }
    53	        cursor += line.len();
    54	    }
    55	    if in_block {
    56	        blocks.push(block(source, block_start, source.len()));
    57	    }
    58	    CstDocument {
    59	        source: source.to_owned(),
    60	        blocks,
    61	    }
    62	}
    63	
    64	/// Emit exact original source bytes.
    65	#[must_use]
    66	pub fn emit(document: &CstDocument) -> &str {
    67	    &document.source
    68	}

    70	fn block(source: &str, start: usize, end: usize) -> OpaqueBlock {
    71	    let text = &source[start..end];
    72	    let first = text.lines().next().unwrap_or_default().trim_start();
    73	    // M17.5 F-62: `#` alone made every hash-prefixed line a heading, including
    74	    // `#!liminal-explicit-v1`, which selects a dialect and is not a heading.
    75	    // `-` alone made `-not-a-list` a list while `*` already required its
    76	    // space. Both now match the formatter's own rule: a marker, then a space.
    77	    let hashes = first.chars().take_while(|ch| *ch == '#').count();
    78	    let heading = hashes > 0 && first[hashes..].starts_with(' ');
    79	    let coarse_kind = if first.starts_with("```") {
    80	        CoarseKind::Fence
    81	    } else if heading {
    82	        CoarseKind::Heading
    83	    } else if first.starts_with("- ") || first.starts_with("* ") {
    84	        CoarseKind::List
    85	    } else if first.starts_with('@') {
    86	        CoarseKind::Directive
    87	    } else if first.starts_with("![") || first.contains("](") {
    88	        CoarseKind::ResourceReference
    89	    } else {
    90	        CoarseKind::ParagraphLike
    91	    };
    92	    OpaqueBlock {
    93	        range: SourceRange {
    94	            start: start as u64,
    95	            end: end as u64,
    96	        },
    97	        hash: ContentHash::of(text.as_bytes()),
    98	        coarse_kind,
    99	    }
   100	}

    79	impl PartialEq for Phase1Document {
    80	    /// Semantic equality: the derived graph, and the HIR with its source
    81	    /// positions removed. Reformatting moves every byte offset, so positions
    82	    /// cannot take part; leaving the HIR out entirely let a reparse drift in
    83	    /// HIR content pass as equal (M17.5 blind pass 1, A02).
    84	    ///
    85	    /// Diagnostics are deliberately NOT part of equality. They describe the
    86	    /// text that was parsed, and canonical emission rewrites that text: a
    87	    /// malformed construct is diagnosed, dropped, and absent from the emitted
    88	    /// source, so the reparse is clean while the HIR and graph are unchanged
    89	    /// (regression fixture `f09-070ba65d68c9.bin`: UnknownForm and
    90	    /// MalformedSyntax on the original, none on the reparse, identical HIR).
    91	    /// A serialization failure compares unequal rather than masking a
    92	    /// difference.
    93	    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
    94	        self.holder == other.holder
    95	            && basis_semantic_eq(&self.graph.basis, &other.graph.basis, &self.holder)
    96	            && self.graph.nodes == other.graph.nodes
    97	            && self.graph.relations == other.graph.relations
    98	            && match (
    99	                serde_json::to_value(&self.hir),
   100	                serde_json::to_value(&other.hir),
   101	            ) {
   102	                (Ok(a), Ok(b)) => position_free(a) == position_free(b),
   103	                _ => false,
   104	            }
   105	    }
   106	}

   108	/// A value's serialization with every source position removed: `range`
   109	/// fields, the source map and the source basis, which all move under
   110	/// reformatting while the meaning stays.
   111	fn position_free(mut json: serde_json::Value) -> serde_json::Value {
   112	    // M17.5 F-61: the strip used to apply to every object at every depth by
   113	    // key name. `HirItem::attributes` is a `BTreeMap<String, HirValue>` whose
   114	    // keys are the author's, so a document carrying an attribute named
   115	    // `range`, `source_map` or `basis` had it removed from both sides and two
   116	    // documents differing only there compared equal — the round-trip and
   117	    // idempotence laws would accept losing that attribute. Position keys are
   118	    // stripped structurally now, never inside a map the author names.
   119	    fn strip(value: &mut serde_json::Value, author_keyed: bool) {
   120	        match value {
   121	            serde_json::Value::Object(map) => {
   122	                if !author_keyed {
   123	                    map.retain(|key, _| !matches!(key.as_str(), "range" | "source_map" | "basis"));
   124	                }
   125	                for (key, child) in map.iter_mut() {
   126	                    // `HirItem::attributes` is the only author-keyed map the
   127	                    // HIR serializes, and `HirValue` has no map variant, so an
   128	                    // author-keyed subtree is exactly one level deep. The test
   129	                    // below locks that; if a second such map appears, it must
   130	                    // be named here too.
   131	                    strip(child, !author_keyed && key == "attributes");
   132	                }
   133	            }
   134	            serde_json::Value::Array(items) => {
   135	                for item in items {
   136	                    strip(item, author_keyed);
   137	                }
   138	            }
   139	            _ => {}
   140	        }
   141	    }
   142	    strip(&mut json, false);
   143	    json
   144	}

   147	fn basis_semantic_eq(a: &WorkspaceBasis, b: &WorkspaceBasis, holder: &JurisdictionKey) -> bool {
   148	    if a.transaction != b.transaction
   149	        || a.perspective != b.perspective
   150	        || a.components.len() != b.components.len()
   151	    {
   152	        return false;
   153	    }
   154	    a.components
   155	        .iter()
   156	        .all(|(key, av)| match (key, b.components.get(key)) {
   157	            (key, Some(bv)) if key == holder => component_address_eq(av, bv),
   158	            (_, Some(bv)) => av == bv,
   159	            _ => false,
   160	        })
   161	}
   162	fn component_address_eq(a: &BasisComponent, b: &BasisComponent) -> bool {
   163	    match (a, b) {
   164	        (
   165	            BasisComponent::FileContent { path: ap, .. },
   166	            BasisComponent::FileContent { path: bp, .. },
   167	        ) => ap == bp,
   168	        (
   169	            BasisComponent::BufferGeneration {
   170	                client: ac,
   171	                buffer: ab,
   172	                epoch: ae,
   173	                generation: ag,
   174	                base_file_hash: ah,
   175	                ..
   176	            },
   177	            BasisComponent::BufferGeneration {
   178	                client: bc,
   179	                buffer: bb,
   180	                epoch: be,
   181	                generation: bg,
   182	                base_file_hash: bh,
   183	                ..
   184	            },
   185	        ) => (ac, ab, ae, ag, ah) == (bc, bb, be, bg, bh),
   186	        _ => a == b,
   187	    }
   188	}

   316	/// Render `hir` in the compact surface, or `None` when any root is not
   317	/// compact-representable.
   318	///
   319	/// The compact surface expresses exactly one shape: a `paragraph` node whose
   320	/// only child is a literal, carrying at most an `id` attribute — i.e. what
   321	/// `alpha {#a}` parses to. Anything richer (relations, nested nodes, ordered
   322	/// blocks, other attributes) has no compact spelling, so the whole document
   323	/// falls back rather than emitting a partial or lossy rendering.
   324	fn emit_compact(hir: &HirDocument) -> Option<String> {
   325	    let items: BTreeMap<liminal_hir::HirId, &HirItem> =
   326	        hir.items.iter().map(|item| (item.id, item)).collect();
   327	
   328	    let mut blocks = Vec::with_capacity(hir.roots.len());
   329	    for root in &hir.roots {
   330	        let item = items.get(root)?;
   331	        let HirItemKind::NodeConstruction { name } = &item.kind else {
   332	            return None;
   333	        };
   334	        if name != "paragraph" || item.children.len() != 1 {
   335	            return None;
   336	        }
   337	        let child = items.get(&item.children[0])?;
   338	        let HirItemKind::Literal { value } = &child.kind else {
   339	            return None;
   340	        };
   341	        if !is_compact_literal(value) {
   342	            return None;
   343	        }
   344	        if !child.attributes.is_empty() || !child.children.is_empty() {
   345	            return None;
   346	        }
   347	
   348	        let id = match item.attributes.len() {
   349	            0 => None,
   350	            1 => match item.attributes.get("id") {
   351	                Some(HirValue::String(id)) if is_compact_id(id) => Some(id.clone()),
   352	                _ => return None,
   353	            },
   354	            _ => return None,
   355	        };
   356	
   357	        blocks.push(match id {
   358	            Some(id) => format!("{value} {{#{id}}}"),
   359	            None => value.clone(),
   360	        });
   361	    }
   362	
   363	    Some(format!("{}\n", blocks.join("\n\n")))
   364	}

   366	/// Compact markers use the same closed identifier grammar as the source
   367	/// parser. Invalid ids must force explicit emission; interpolating one into a
   368	/// marker would make a format/parse round trip lossy.
   369	fn is_compact_id(id: &str) -> bool {
   370	    !id.is_empty()
   371	        && id
   372	            .bytes()
   373	            .all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(byte, b'_' | b'-'))
   374	}

   376	/// Compact paragraphs are maximal runs of non-blank lines. Empty, blank-line,
   377	/// or CR-containing literals would be split, dropped, or normalized by the
   378	/// compact parser, so they must use explicit emission.
   379	fn is_compact_literal(value: &str) -> bool {
   380	    if value.trim().is_empty()
   381	        || value.contains('\r')
   382	        || value.ends_with('\n')
   383	        || value.lines().any(|line| line.trim().is_empty())
   384	    {
   385	        return false;
   386	    }
   387	
   388	    // The compact parser has a second projection layer beyond paragraph
   389	    // splitting: durable markers, headings, fences, quotes, and lists all
   390	    // change the resulting HIR. A literal carrying any of those spellings
   391	    // must use explicit emission or the formatter silently changes meaning.
   392	    let blocks = paragraph::parse(value);
   393	    if blocks.len() != 1 || blocks[0].id.is_some() || blocks[0].text != value {
   394	        return false;
   395	    }
   396	    let lines = value.lines().collect::<Vec<_>>();
   397	    let first = lines[0];
   398	    let first_trimmed = first.trim_start();
   399	    let heading = first_trimmed.chars().take_while(|ch| *ch == '#').count();
   400	    let heading_end = first_trimmed
   401	        .char_indices()
   402	        .nth(heading)
   403	        .map_or(first_trimmed.len(), |(index, _)| index);
   404	    if (heading > 0
   405	        && first_trimmed
   406	            .get(heading_end..)
   407	            .is_some_and(|rest| rest.starts_with(' ')))
   408	        || first_trimmed.starts_with("```")
   409	        // M17.5 F-61: `lower` picks the dialect by whether the source starts
   410	        // with this marker, and `#!` is not `# `, so the heading exclusion
   411	        // never saw it. A literal spelling it, emitted compactly, comes back
   412	        // as an explicit-dialect document — a different HIR from the same
   413	        // bytes, which is the projection this whole list exists to refuse.
   414	        || first_trimmed.starts_with(liminal_hir::EXPLICIT_DIALECT_MARKER)
   415	        || lines.iter().all(|line| line.trim_start().starts_with('>'))
   416	        || lines
   417	            .iter()
   418	            .all(|line| line.trim_start().starts_with("- ") || line.trim_start().starts_with("* "))
   419	        || (lines.iter().all(|line| {
   420	            line.trim_start()
   421	                .chars()
   422	                .next()
   423	                .is_some_and(|ch| ch.is_ascii_digit())
   424	        }) && lines.iter().all(|line| line.contains(". ")))
   425	    {
   426	        return false;
   427	    }
   428	    true
   429	}

   431	fn emit_item(
   432	    out: &mut String,
   433	    item: &HirItem,
   434	    items: &BTreeMap<liminal_hir::HirId, &HirItem>,
   435	    depth: usize,
   436	) -> Result<(), Phase1FormatError> {
   437	    let indent = "  ".repeat(depth);
   438	    match &item.kind {
   439	        HirItemKind::Literal { value } => {
   440	            out.push_str(&format!("{indent}literal {};\n", json_string(value)))
   441	        }
   442	        HirItemKind::NodeConstruction { name } => {
   443	            out.push_str(&format!("{indent}node {name}"));
   444	            emit_attrs(out, &item.attributes)?;
   445	            if item.children.is_empty() {
   446	                out.push_str(";\n");
   447	            } else {
   448	                out.push_str(" {\n");
   449	                for child in &item.children {
   450	                    emit_item(
   451	                        out,
   452	                        items.get(child).ok_or_else(|| {
   453	                            Phase1FormatError::Emit(format!("dangling child {child:?}"))
   454	                        })?,
   455	                        items,
   456	                        depth + 1,
   457	                    )?;
   458	                }
   459	                out.push_str(&format!("{indent}}}\n"));
   460	            }
   461	        }
   462	        HirItemKind::RelationConstruction {
   463	            source,
   464	            kind,
   465	            target,
   466	        } => {
   467	            out.push_str(&format!(
   468	                "{indent}relation {} -[{kind}]-> {}",
   469	                ref_text(source),
   470	                ref_text(target)
   471	            ));
   472	            emit_attrs(out, &item.attributes)?;
   473	            out.push_str(";\n");
   474	        }
   475	        HirItemKind::AttributeAssignment { name, value, .. } => out.push_str(&format!(
   476	            "{indent}attribute {name} = {};\n",
   477	            value_text(value)
   478	        )),
   479	        HirItemKind::OrderedBlock => {
   480	            // M17.5 F-21: an EMPTY ordered block used to emit `ordered;`, and
   481	            // M19's grammar has no such form — `ordered = "ordered", spacing,
   482	            // block`, with the block mandatory. The parser therefore read
   483	            // `ordered;` back as the literal string "ordered;", so
   484	            // `parse(emit(parse(x))) != parse(x)` for any document containing an
   485	            // empty ordered block. The block is always emitted now, empty or not.
   486	            //
   487	            // `node` is deliberately NOT changed alongside it. `node foo;` is the
   488	            // same grammar deviation, but the parser accepts a block-less node
   489	            // and reproduces it exactly, so it round-trips. Tightening the parser
   490	            // to match the grammar there is M19's call, not a fix this lane needs.
   491	            out.push_str(&format!("{indent}ordered"));
   492	            {
   493	                out.push_str(" {\n");
   494	                for child in &item.children {
   495	                    emit_item(
   496	                        out,
   497	                        items.get(child).ok_or_else(|| {
   498	                            Phase1FormatError::Emit(format!("dangling child {child:?}"))
   499	                        })?,
   500	                        items,
   501	                        depth + 1,
   502	                    )?;
   503	                }
   504	                out.push_str(&format!("{indent}}}\n"));
   505	            }
   506	        }
   507	        HirItemKind::Reference { target } => {
   508	            out.push_str(&format!("{indent}reference {};\n", ref_text(target)))
   509	        }
   510	        HirItemKind::Expression { source } => {
   511	            out.push_str(&format!("{indent}expression {};\n", json_string(source)))
   512	        }
   513	        HirItemKind::MacroInvocation { name, arguments } => out.push_str(&format!(
   514	            "{indent}macro {name}({});\n",
   515	            arguments
   516	                .iter()
   517	                .map(value_text)
   518	                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
   519	                .join(", ")
   520	        )),
   521	    }
   522	    Ok(())
   523	}
   524	fn emit_attrs(
   525	    out: &mut String,
   526	    attrs: &BTreeMap<String, HirValue>,
   527	) -> Result<(), Phase1FormatError> {
   528	    if !attrs.is_empty() {
   529	        out.push_str(" (");
   530	        out.push_str(
   531	            &attrs
   532	                .iter()
   533	                .map(|(k, v)| format!("{k} = {}", value_text(v)))
   534	                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
   535	                .join(", "),
   536	        );
   537	        out.push(')');
   538	    }
   539	    Ok(())
   540	}
   541	fn json_string(value: &str) -> String {
   542	    serde_json::to_string(value).unwrap_or_else(|_| "\"\"".to_owned())
   543	}
   544	fn ref_text(value: &HirReference) -> String {
   545	    match value {
   546	        HirReference::Resolved(id) => format!("@hir{}", id.0),
   547	        HirReference::Unresolved(name) => format!("@{name}"),
   548	    }
   549	}
   550	fn value_text(value: &HirValue) -> String {
   551	    match value {
   552	        HirValue::Null => "null".into(),
   553	        HirValue::Bool(v) => v.to_string(),
   554	        HirValue::Integer(v) => v.to_string(),
   555	        HirValue::String(v) => json_string(v),
   556	        HirValue::Reference(r) => ref_text(r),
   557	        HirValue::List(values) => format!(
   558	            "[{}]",
   559	            values.iter().map(value_text).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
   560	        ),
   561	    }
   562	}

   564	/// Deterministic paragraph-compatible renderer kept for existing HTML tests.
   565	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
   566	pub struct MarkdownRenderer;
   567	impl MarkdownRenderer {
   568	    pub fn render(&self, source: &str) -> Result<String, MarkdownError> {
   569	        self.render_blocks(&paragraph::parse(source))
   570	    }
   571	    pub fn render_blocks(&self, blocks: &[Block]) -> Result<String, MarkdownError> {
   572	        let mut out = String::from("<article>\n");
   573	        for block in blocks {
   574	            let id = block
   575	                .id
   576	                .as_deref()
   577	                .map(|v| format!(" data-node-id=\"{}\"", escape_html(v)))
   578	                .unwrap_or_default();
   579	            let text = escape_html(&block.text).replace('\n', "<br />\n");
   580	            out.push_str(&format!("<p{id}>{text}</p>\n"));
   581	        }
   582	        out.push_str("</article>\n");
   583	        Ok(out)
   584	    }
   585	}
   586	fn escape_html(input: &str) -> String {
   587	    input
   588	        .chars()
   589	        .map(|ch| match ch {
   590	            '&' => "&".into(),
   591	            '<' => "<".into(),
   592	            '>' => ">".into(),
   593	            '"' => """.into(),
   594	            '\'' => "'".into(),
   595	            _ => ch.to_string(),
   596	        })
   597	        .collect()
   598	}

   600	/// Generic formatter seam.
   601	pub trait Formatter {
   602	    type Doc;
   603	    type Error;
   604	    fn parse(&self, source: &str) -> Result<Self::Doc, Self::Error>;
   605	    fn emit(&self, doc: &Self::Doc) -> Result<String, Self::Error>;
   606	    fn format(&self, source: &str) -> Result<String, Self::Error>;
   607	
   608	    /// Emit `doc` in a REQUESTED surface dialect (AM-17.3, additive).
   609	    ///
   610	    /// [`emit`](Formatter::emit) is the canonical projection and always
   611	    /// produces the explicit surface; this is the dialect-aware counterpart
   612	    /// M19's "canonical round-trip across compact and explicit" and M20's
   613	    /// `lim fmt` need — a formatter that rewrote a reader's compact document
   614	    /// into `#!liminal-explicit-v1` on every save would destroy the surface
   615	    /// they chose.
   616	    ///
   617	    /// The default implementation delegates to `emit`, so this addition
   618	    /// cannot change the behavior of any existing implementor. An
   619	    /// implementation that cannot express `doc` in `dialect` MUST fall back
   620	    /// to the canonical surface rather than emit a lossy approximation.
   621	    ///
   622	    /// # Errors
   623	    /// Whatever the underlying emission reports.
   624	    fn emit_in_dialect(
   625	        &self,
   626	        doc: &Self::Doc,
   627	        dialect: SourceDialect,
   628	    ) -> Result<String, Self::Error> {
   629	        let _ = dialect;
   630	        self.emit(doc)
   631	    }
   632	}

     1	//! Pure incremental queries over an explicit Workspace Basis.
     2	//!
     3	//! Every expensive pure computation is a revisioned query over a declared
     4	//! [`WorkspaceBasis`]: deterministic for that basis, immutable, memoized,
     5	//! dependency-tracked, and replayable from frozen Jurisdiction inputs
     6	//! (v4 §24). External resolution is deliberately absent: a resolver performs
     7	//! effects OUTSIDE the query engine and submits a new Jurisdiction
     8	//! transaction; pure queries then consume that accepted input (v4 §24, §8.6).
     9	//! This is the Salsa boundary adopted verbatim — pure tracked queries versus
    10	//! external input mutation, extended with Workspace Basis and freshness
    11	//! rather than performing effects inside queries (v4 §118A).
    12	//!
    13	//! **RESERVED — implementation begins Phase -1.3** (v4 Part XXII), where the
    14	//! revision/Basis/invalidation prototype promotes a tiny pure query layer.
    15	//! No memoization, no Salsa dependency, no parallel scheduling before then
    16	//! (Law 14: interpretive reference semantics only).
    17	//!
    18	//! This crate exists now so the constitutional vocabulary has a compiled,
    19	//! greppable home: the trait seams below let the §112 correctness laws
    20	//! (`incremental_compile(x, edits) ≡ full_compile(apply(x, edits))`) compile
    21	//! as generic functions in the conformance suite today, years before the
    22	//! first real implementation plugs in.
    23

    37	    /// Inclusive byte start in original source.
    38	    pub start: usize,

    45	/// Bounded paragraph compiler used by Phase 1 equivalence laws.
    46	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
    47	pub struct ParagraphCompiler;
    48	
    49	impl IncrementalCompiler for ParagraphCompiler {
    50	    type Source = String;
    51	    type Edit = SourceEdit;
    52	    type Output = Vec<Block>;
    53	
    54	    fn full(&self, source: &Self::Source, _basis: &WorkspaceBasis) -> Self::Output {
    55	        paragraph::parse(source)
    56	    }
    57	
    58	    fn apply(&self, source: &Self::Source, edits: &[Self::Edit]) -> Self::Source {
    59	        let mut output = source.clone();
    60	        let mut ordered = edits
    61	            .iter()

   107	    fn incremental(

   122	/// Independently scan the tiny paragraph grammar used as the Phase 1
   123	/// incremental oracle. This intentionally does not call `paragraph::parse`.
   124	fn incremental_paragraph_oracle(input: &str) -> Vec<Block> {
   125	    let line_starts = std::iter::once(0)
   126	        .chain(input.match_indices('\n').map(|(offset, _)| offset + 1))
   127	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
   128	    let mut blocks = Vec::new();
   129	    let mut current_lines = Vec::new();
   130	    let mut block_start = None;
   131	    let mut block_end = 0;
   132	
   133	    for (line_index, line) in input.lines().enumerate() {
   134	        if line.trim().is_empty() {
   135	            if let Some(start) = block_start.take() {
   136	                blocks.push(build_oracle_block(&current_lines, start, block_end));
   137	                current_lines.clear();
   138	            }
   139	            continue;
   140	        }
   141	
   142	        let line_start = line_starts[line_index];
   143	        block_start.get_or_insert(line_start);
   144	        block_end = line_start + line.len();
   145	        current_lines.push(line);
   146	    }
   147	
   148	    if let Some(start) = block_start {
   149	        blocks.push(build_oracle_block(&current_lines, start, block_end));
   150	    }

   152	    blocks
   153	}

   155	fn build_oracle_block(lines: &[&str], start: usize, end: usize) -> Block {
   156	    let last_line = lines.last().expect("oracle blocks are non-empty");
   157	    let (id, cleaned_last_line) = extract_oracle_marker(last_line);
   158	    let mut text_lines = lines.to_vec();
   159	
   160	    if let Some(cleaned) = cleaned_last_line.as_deref() {
   161	        if cleaned.is_empty() {
   162	            text_lines.pop();
   163	        } else {
   164	            *text_lines.last_mut().expect("oracle blocks are non-empty") = cleaned;
   165	        }
   166	    }
   167	
   168	    Block {
   169	        text: text_lines.join("\n"),
   170	        id,
   171	        range: SourceRange {
   172	            start: start as u64,
   173	            end: end as u64,
   174	        },
   175	    }
   176	}

   178	/// Independently implement paragraph's terminal `{#id}` grammar.
   179	fn extract_oracle_marker(line: &str) -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {
   180	    let Some(marker_start) = line.rfind("{#") else {
   181	        return (None, None);
   182	    };
   183	    let marker = &line[marker_start + 2..];
   184	    let Some(close) = marker.find('}') else {
   185	        return (None, None);
   186	    };
   187	    let id = &marker[..close];
   188	
   189	    if id.is_empty()
   190	        || !id
   191	            .chars()
   192	            .all(|character| character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(character, '-' | '_'))
   193	        || !marker[close + 1..].trim().is_empty()
   194	    {
   195	        return (None, None);
   196	    }
   197	
   198	    let cleaned = line[..marker_start].trim_end().to_owned();
   199	    (Some(id.to_owned()), Some(cleaned))
   200	}

   202	/// A pure revisioned computation over a declared Workspace Basis (v4 §24).
   203	///
   204	/// SHAPE PROVISIONAL — this seam exists so §112 laws and the conformance
   205	/// harness compile as generics now; Phase -1.3/0 may reshape it freely.
   206	///
   207	/// Contract (v4 §24): results are deterministic for a declared basis and
   208	/// immutable once produced. Implementations must record every Basis component
   209	/// they read into `deps` — component-granular dependency tracking is what
   210	/// makes precise invalidation possible (v4 §7.5; R4 §10 "buffer generations
   211	/// invalidate only dependent queries"). Effects are forbidden inside
   212	/// `execute` (v4 §8.6, §118A).
   213	pub trait Query {
   214	    /// The immutable query result.
   215	    type Output;
   216	
   217	    /// Execute the query at `basis`, recording every component read into
   218	    /// `deps` (v4 §24 "dependency tracking", "precise invalidation").
   219	    fn execute(&self, basis: &WorkspaceBasis, deps: &mut ComponentDeps) -> Self::Output;
   220	}
   221	
   222	/// The incremental-equals-full compilation seam (v4 §112).
   223	///
   224	/// SHAPE PROVISIONAL — exists only so the §112 law compiles as a generic
   225	/// conformance test now; Phase -1.3/1 may reshape it freely.
   226	///
   227	/// Law (v4 §112): at the same Basis,
   228	/// `incremental(x, edits)` must equal `full(apply(x, edits))` —
   229	/// an incremental compile may never diverge from the from-scratch compile of
   230	/// the edited source. `Output: PartialEq` exists precisely so the law is
   231	/// checkable, and so unchanged results can stop invalidation cascades
   232	/// (v4 §24 "equality checks to prevent cascading unchanged results").
   233	pub trait IncrementalCompiler {
   234	    /// The source representation being compiled.
   235	    type Source;
   236	    /// One edit applicable to the source.
   237	    type Edit;
   238	    /// The compilation result; `PartialEq` so the §112 law is checkable.
   239	    type Output: PartialEq;
   240	
   241	    /// Compile `source` from scratch at `basis`.
   242	    fn full(&self, source: &Self::Source, basis: &WorkspaceBasis) -> Self::Output;
   243	
   244	    /// Apply `edits` to `source`, producing the edited source.
   245	    fn apply(&self, source: &Self::Source, edits: &[Self::Edit]) -> Self::Source;
   246	
   247	    /// Incrementally recompile `source` under `edits` at `basis`.
   248	    ///
   249	    /// Must equal `self.full(&self.apply(source, edits), basis)` (v4 §112).
   250	    fn incremental(
   251	        &self,
   252	        source: &Self::Source,
   253	        edits: &[Self::Edit],
   254	        basis: &WorkspaceBasis,
   255	    ) -> Self::Output;
   256	}

     1	# 0020. Require high-assurance Phase 1 suite qualification
     2	
     3	- **Status:** accepted
     4	- **Date:** 2026-07-20
     5	- **Deciders:** Brian
     6	- **Related:** M17; `docs/execution/phase1-suite-review.md`; v4 Part XXII Phase 1;

     8	
     9	## Context
    10	
    11	M17 already requires a proposed Phase 1 suite, coverage matrices, mutation and
    12	fuzz evidence, and two independent adversarial passes. Those nouns do not set a
    13	qualification bar. A suite can claim each artifact while using trivial mutants,
    14	short fuzz runs, shared oracles, vacuous predicates, or reviews that contaminate
    15	one another.
    16	
    17	Phase 1 will freeze foundations used by later parsers, graph projections,
    18	recovery, revision tracking, and external adapters. Test quantity is therefore
    19	not enough. Ratification needs evidence that the suite detects seeded defects,
    20	survives malformed state, reproduces failures, and has no unexamined critical
    21	requirement. The campaign must remain finite so it can be repeated after fixes.
    22	
    23	## Decision
    24	
    25	Phase 1 suite ratification SHALL use the **HAQP-1 high-assurance qualification
    26	profile** below. Passing HAQP-1 does not ratify the suite; it only makes the
    27	proposed packet eligible for Brian's separate T1 ratification decision.
    28	
    29	### 1. Two execution lanes
    30	
    31	- The **continuous lane** runs deterministic unit, integration, regression,
    32	  malformed-input, and gate-canary tests on ordinary changes. It includes
    33	  `just ci` and must not depend on elapsed-time fuzz success.
    34	- The **qualification lane** runs from one fixed clean commit and source tree.
    35	  It contains every HAQP-1 item and is rerun in full after the last verified
    36	  defect is fixed. Partial reruns are diagnostic evidence only.
    37	- Every command, exact toolchain and dependency version, lockfile hash, target,
    38	  seed, declared non-locked regression/fuzz corpus hash, environment
    39	  classification, exit status, and raw artifact hash is recorded. Missing
    40	  evidence fails closed.
    41	
    42	#### Qualification provenance amendment (2026-08-12)
    43	
    44	The qualification packet is committed after its fixed-base campaign. Its
    45	provenance records the campaign commit and that commit's tree hash. The
    46	qualification commit MUST have exactly that campaign commit as its first
    47	parent; the verifier checks parent and tree hashes, requires a clean tree, and
    48	rejects any other provenance shape. This parent-binding design avoids a
    49	self-referential packet commit hash while keeping evidence tied to one clean
    50	source tree. No external manifest or signing key is required.
    51	
    52	### 2. Bidirectional requirements traceability
    53	
    54	- Every Phase 1 normative law, `MUST`, threat boundary, abuse case, fault class,
    55	  work-order exit criterion, and ratification gate has a stable requirement ID.
    56	- Every ID maps to at least one test, and every test maps back to at least one
    57	  ID. Machine verification rejects duplicates, orphans, unknown IDs, and missing
    58	  critical rows.
    59	- Every applicable law has positive, negative, malformed/adversarial,
    60	  basis/provenance, and deterministic-replay evidence. Stateful laws also have
    61	  injected-fault and idempotent-recovery evidence.
    62	- Uncovered critical rows cannot be waived inside the packet. Any exception is
    63	  an exact coordinate accepted through a separate T1 amendment; wildcards,
    64	  whole-file exclusions, and substring allowances are forbidden.
    65	
    66	### 3. Tests of the tests
    67	
    68	- Qualification predeclares at least **64 semantic mutants** across critical
    69	  surfaces. Operators include predicate deletion/inversion, threshold ±1,
    70	  missing enum or kind dispatch, success/error substitution, stale-Basis
    71	  acceptance, wrong Holder/profile selection, skipped durable transition,
    72	  disabled crash point, ordering nondeterminism, oracle short-circuit, and
    73	  broadened allow-list.
    74	- Every critical surface family receives at least eight mutants, and no single
    75	  operator supplies more than one quarter of the denominator. Mutation selection
    76	  cannot cluster around easy-to-kill utility paths.
    77	- Mutation score is **100% of applicable, non-duplicate, non-equivalent
    78	  mutants**. One survivor blocks eligibility.
    79	- An equivalent or duplicate disposition names the mutant, shows the proof, and
    80	  receives concurring verification in both adversarial-pass records. Disposed
    81	  mutants remain visible in the numerator/denominator report.
    82	- Every ratification gate and every M17 Level-3 measurement conjunct gets at
    83	  least one disposable gate canary: a deliberate violation must make the exact
    84	  expected gate fail. Canary execution occurs outside the working tree and
    85	  restores the fixed review base afterward.
    86	
    87	### 4. Generated, metamorphic, and fuzz evidence
    88	
    89	- Five critical surface families each execute at least **100,000 accepted
    90	  deterministic generated cases** from recorded seeds: source/CST/formatting,
    91	  graph/interchange codecs, transforms/projections, repair/ILRP/recovery, and
    92	  Basis/revision/query invalidation.
    93	- Generator attempts and discards are recorded. Discard rate above one percent,
    94	  post-failure filtering, or shrinking the declared domain fails qualification.
    95	- Each family defines independent metamorphic relations where applicable:
    96	  canonical reparse, idempotent replay, inverse/undo, irrelevant-input
    97	  invariance, commuting independent transactions, incremental/full equivalence,
    98	  and deterministic permutation. A relation is not proved by calling the
    99	  implementation's own equality or normalization path on both sides.
   100	- Each family also receives one **30-minute sanitizer-enabled fuzz campaign**
   101	  with at least 16 predeclared seeds spanning valid, boundary, truncated,
   102	  malformed, and hostile input. Total fuzz budget is at least 150 target-minutes.
   103	- Every crash, panic, timeout, memory error, divergence, or minimized failure is
   104	  a failing result. Minimized artifacts become named regression fixtures before
   105	  the qualification lane is rerun.
   106	- Concurrent code receives deterministic schedule exploration. If Phase 1 adds
   107	  no concurrent implementation, the packet records the condition as not
   108	  applicable rather than fabricating coverage.
   109	
   110	### 5. Oracle and fault independence
   111	
   112	- Incremental and full-reparse oracles may share raw bytes and published data
   113	  schemas only. They may not share parser events, lowering code, canonicalizers,
   114	  anchor recovery, comparison shortcuts, or expected-result construction.
   115	- Expected values come from fixed literals, worked spec examples, or a separately
   116	  implemented oracle. Self-snapshots generated by the system under test are not
   117	  authority without independent verification.
   118	- Every registered durable-transition crash boundary is injected immediately
   119	  before and after the transition. Recovery runs twice and must reach the same
   120	  terminal state without hidden staged data, duplicate effects, or mixed Basis.
   121	- Fault matrix is exhaustive over registered boundaries. Runtime discovery and
   122	  declared inventory must match exactly; either-side drift fails.
   123	
   124	### 6. Independent adversarial review
   125	
   126	- Pass 1 attacks implementation and packet for vacuity, shared-oracle coupling,
   127	  missing negatives, weak mutants, fault omissions, nondeterminism, corpus
   128	  leakage, exception broadening, and evidence/report drift.
   129	- Pass 2 starts from the original spec and fixed review base. It cannot read Pass
   130	  1 prompts, findings, dispositions, or fixes until it records its own findings.
   131	- Passes use distinct reviewer identities and isolated conversation/session
   132	  state. If both reviewers are automated, they use different model families;
   133	  otherwise at least one reviewer is human. Sanitized prompt and reviewer
   134	  identity hashes are recorded without credentials or secret material.
   135	- Each pass records at least 12 concrete falsification attempts, including
   136	  attempted violations that the suite correctly catches. Findings cite exact
   137	  evidence and are independently reproduced before any fix.
   138	- Zero verified findings may remain unresolved. False positives remain recorded
   139	  with reproduction evidence; they are not silently deleted.
   140	
   141	### 7. Bounded campaign and residual risk
   142	
   143	- HAQP-1 qualification is a review-candidate campaign, not a per-edit tax. Its
   144	  intended wall-clock ceiling is eight hours on the recorded reference machine.
   145	  Crossing that ceiling twice blocks ratification and triggers a superseding ADR
   146	  or harness optimization; thresholds cannot be silently reduced.
   147	- Packet lists every known limitation with owner, severity, trigger, affected
   148	  requirement, evidence, and planned resolution phase. "Future work" without
   149	  those coordinates is invalid.
   150	- Locked acceptance corpora remain black-box inputs touched only by existing
   151	  approved verifiers. HAQP-1 does not authorize inspecting, listing, copying,
   152	  hashing, or deriving new fixtures from locked corpus contents.
   153	
   154	**What would falsify or reverse this:** two clean qualification attempts exceed
   155	the eight-hour ceiling, required tooling cannot produce reproducible evidence,
   156	or HAQP-1 encourages equivalent-mutant or low-value-case inflation without
   157	finding real seeded defects. Reversal requires a superseding ADR with measured
   158	campaign data and cannot weaken already-recorded failures or erase artifacts.
   159	
   160	## Consequences
   161	
   162	- **Positive:** ratification evidence demonstrates sensitivity, independence,
   163	  replayability, traceability, and fault coverage instead of test count alone.
   164	- **Negative:** final qualification consumes up to eight hours, requires at
   165	  least 64 reviewed mutants and 150 target-minutes of fuzzing, and makes every
   166	  post-campaign defect fix trigger another full run.
   167	- **Follow-ups:** AM-17.1 binds M17's packet gate and review records to HAQP-1.
   168	  Phase 1 work orders must budget both execution lanes without ratifying the
   169	  suite automatically.
   170	
   171	## Alternatives considered
   172	
   173	- **Coverage percentages plus ordinary CI** — rejected because high line or
   174	  branch coverage does not show that assertions detect semantic defects.
   175	- **Unbounded fuzzing and exhaustive model checking** — rejected because results
   176	  cannot be repeated on a review schedule and termination becomes subjective.
   177	- **Broad source-wide mutation testing** — rejected because utility-code mutants
   178	  inflate cost and score while diluting critical contract coverage.

     1	//! Pure incremental queries over an explicit Workspace Basis.
     2	//!
     3	//! Every expensive pure computation is a revisioned query over a declared
     4	//! [`WorkspaceBasis`]: deterministic for that basis, immutable, memoized,
     5	//! dependency-tracked, and replayable from frozen Jurisdiction inputs
     6	//! (v4 §24). External resolution is deliberately absent: a resolver performs
     7	//! effects OUTSIDE the query engine and submits a new Jurisdiction
     8	//! transaction; pure queries then consume that accepted input (v4 §24, §8.6).
     9	//! This is the Salsa boundary adopted verbatim — pure tracked queries versus
    10	//! external input mutation, extended with Workspace Basis and freshness
    11	//! rather than performing effects inside queries (v4 §118A).
    12	//!
    13	//! **RESERVED — implementation begins Phase -1.3** (v4 Part XXII), where the
    14	//! revision/Basis/invalidation prototype promotes a tiny pure query layer.
    15	//! No memoization, no Salsa dependency, no parallel scheduling before then
    16	//! (Law 14: interpretive reference semantics only).
    17	//!
    18	//! This crate exists now so the constitutional vocabulary has a compiled,
    19	//! greppable home: the trait seams below let the §112 correctness laws
    20	//! (`incremental_compile(x, edits) ≡ full_compile(apply(x, edits))`) compile
    21	//! as generic functions in the conformance suite today, years before the
    22	//! first real implementation plugs in.
    23

    34	/// UTF-8 byte edit used by the Phase 1 incremental compiler.
    35	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    36	pub struct SourceEdit {
    37	    /// Inclusive byte start in original source.
    38	    pub start: usize,
    39	    /// Exclusive byte end in original source.
    40	    pub end: usize,
    41	    /// Replacement text.
    42	    pub replacement: String,
    43	}

    45	/// Bounded paragraph compiler used by Phase 1 equivalence laws.
    46	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
    47	pub struct ParagraphCompiler;
    48	
    49	impl IncrementalCompiler for ParagraphCompiler {
    50	    type Source = String;
    51	    type Edit = SourceEdit;
    52	    type Output = Vec<Block>;
    53	
    54	    fn full(&self, source: &Self::Source, _basis: &WorkspaceBasis) -> Self::Output {
    55	        paragraph::parse(source)
    56	    }
    57	
    58	    fn apply(&self, source: &Self::Source, edits: &[Self::Edit]) -> Self::Source {
    59	        let mut output = source.clone();
    60	        let mut ordered = edits
    61	            .iter()
    62	            .filter_map(|edit| {
    63	                (edit.start <= edit.end
    64	                    && edit.end <= source.len()
    65	                    && source.is_char_boundary(edit.start)
    66	                    && source.is_char_boundary(edit.end))
    67	                .then_some((edit.start, edit.end, edit.replacement.as_str()))
    68	            })
    69	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    70	        ordered.sort_by(|left, right| right.0.cmp(&left.0).then(right.1.cmp(&left.1)));
    71	
    72	        for index in 0..ordered.len() {
    73	            let (start, end, replacement) = ordered[index];
    74	            // Edits use original-source offsets. Overlapping edits have no
    75	            // deterministic sequential meaning, so discard every member of
    76	            // an overlap set fail-closed.
    77	            let overlaps =
    78	                ordered
    79	                    .iter()
    80	                    .enumerate()
    81	                    .any(|(other, &(other_start, other_end, _))| {
    82	                        if other == index {
    83	                            return false;
    84	                        }
    85	                        // Empty edits are insertions at an original offset.
    86	                        // Two insertions at one offset, or an insertion on a
    87	                        // replacement boundary, have no deterministic order;
    88	                        // reject the whole overlap set fail-closed.
    89	                        if start == end && other_start == other_end {
    90	                            start == other_start
    91	                        } else if start == end {
    92	                            other_start <= start && start <= other_end
    93	                        } else if other_start == other_end {
    94	                            start <= other_start && other_start <= end
    95	                        } else {
    96	                            start < other_end && other_start < end
    97	                        }
    98	                    });
    99	            if overlaps {
   100	                continue;
   101	            }
   102	            output.replace_range(start..end, replacement);
   103	        }
   104	        output
   105	    }
   106	
   107	    fn incremental(
   108	        &self,
   109	        source: &Self::Source,
   110	        edits: &[Self::Edit],
   111	        basis: &WorkspaceBasis,
   112	    ) -> Self::Output {
   113	        // Keep this deliberately independent from `full`: equivalence tests
   114	        // need an oracle capable of exposing a divergence in the canonical
   115	        // parser rather than merely calling it twice.
   116	        let edited = self.apply(source, edits);
   117	        let _ = basis;
   118	        incremental_paragraph_oracle(&edited)
   119	    }
   120	}

   122	/// Independently scan the tiny paragraph grammar used as the Phase 1
   123	/// incremental oracle. This intentionally does not call `paragraph::parse`.
   124	fn incremental_paragraph_oracle(input: &str) -> Vec<Block> {
   125	    let line_starts = std::iter::once(0)
   126	        .chain(input.match_indices('\n').map(|(offset, _)| offset + 1))
   127	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
   128	    let mut blocks = Vec::new();
   129	    let mut current_lines = Vec::new();
   130	    let mut block_start = None;
   131	    let mut block_end = 0;
   132	
   133	    for (line_index, line) in input.lines().enumerate() {
   134	        if line.trim().is_empty() {
   135	            if let Some(start) = block_start.take() {
   136	                blocks.push(build_oracle_block(&current_lines, start, block_end));
   137	                current_lines.clear();
   138	            }
   139	            continue;
   140	        }
   141	
   142	        let line_start = line_starts[line_index];
   143	        block_start.get_or_insert(line_start);
   144	        block_end = line_start + line.len();
   145	        current_lines.push(line);
   146	    }
   147	
   148	    if let Some(start) = block_start {
   149	        blocks.push(build_oracle_block(&current_lines, start, block_end));
   150	    }
   151	
   152	    blocks
   153	}
   154	
   155	fn build_oracle_block(lines: &[&str], start: usize, end: usize) -> Block {
   156	    let last_line = lines.last().expect("oracle blocks are non-empty");
   157	    let (id, cleaned_last_line) = extract_oracle_marker(last_line);
   158	    let mut text_lines = lines.to_vec();
   159	
   160	    if let Some(cleaned) = cleaned_last_line.as_deref() {
   161	        if cleaned.is_empty() {
   162	            text_lines.pop();
   163	        } else {
   164	            *text_lines.last_mut().expect("oracle blocks are non-empty") = cleaned;
   165	        }
   166	    }
   167	
   168	    Block {
   169	        text: text_lines.join("\n"),
   170	        id,
   171	        range: SourceRange {
   172	            start: start as u64,
   173	            end: end as u64,
   174	        },
   175	    }
   176	}
   177	
   178	/// Independently implement paragraph's terminal `{#id}` grammar.
   179	fn extract_oracle_marker(line: &str) -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {
   180	    let Some(marker_start) = line.rfind("{#") else {
   181	        return (None, None);
   182	    };
   183	    let marker = &line[marker_start + 2..];
   184	    let Some(close) = marker.find('}') else {
   185	        return (None, None);
   186	    };
   187	    let id = &marker[..close];
   188	
   189	    if id.is_empty()
   190	        || !id
   191	            .chars()
   192	            .all(|character| character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(character, '-' | '_'))
   193	        || !marker[close + 1..].trim().is_empty()
   194	    {
   195	        return (None, None);
   196	    }
   197	
   198	    let cleaned = line[..marker_start].trim_end().to_owned();
   199	    (Some(id.to_owned()), Some(cleaned))
   200	}

   202	/// A pure revisioned computation over a declared Workspace Basis (v4 §24).
   203	///
   204	/// SHAPE PROVISIONAL — this seam exists so §112 laws and the conformance
   205	/// harness compile as generics now; Phase -1.3/0 may reshape it freely.
   206	///
   207	/// Contract (v4 §24): results are deterministic for a declared basis and
   208	/// immutable once produced. Implementations must record every Basis component
   209	/// they read into `deps` — component-granular dependency tracking is what
   210	/// makes precise invalidation possible (v4 §7.5; R4 §10 "buffer generations
   211	/// invalidate only dependent queries"). Effects are forbidden inside
   212	/// `execute` (v4 §8.6, §118A).
   213	pub trait Query {
   214	    /// The immutable query result.
   215	    type Output;
   216	
   217	    /// Execute the query at `basis`, recording every component read into
   218	    /// `deps` (v4 §24 "dependency tracking", "precise invalidation").
   219	    fn execute(&self, basis: &WorkspaceBasis, deps: &mut ComponentDeps) -> Self::Output;
   220	}
   221	
   222	/// The incremental-equals-full compilation seam (v4 §112).
   223	///
   224	/// SHAPE PROVISIONAL — exists only so the §112 law compiles as a generic
   225	/// conformance test now; Phase -1.3/1 may reshape it freely.
   226	///
   227	/// Law (v4 §112): at the same Basis,
   228	/// `incremental(x, edits)` must equal `full(apply(x, edits))` —
   229	/// an incremental compile may never diverge from the from-scratch compile of
   230	/// the edited source. `Output: PartialEq` exists precisely so the law is
   231	/// checkable, and so unchanged results can stop invalidation cascades
   232	/// (v4 §24 "equality checks to prevent cascading unchanged results").
   233	pub trait IncrementalCompiler {
   234	    /// The source representation being compiled.
   235	    type Source;
   236	    /// One edit applicable to the source.
   237	    type Edit;
   238	    /// The compilation result; `PartialEq` so the §112 law is checkable.
   239	    type Output: PartialEq;
   240	
   241	    /// Compile `source` from scratch at `basis`.
   242	    fn full(&self, source: &Self::Source, basis: &WorkspaceBasis) -> Self::Output;
   243	
   244	    /// Apply `edits` to `source`, producing the edited source.
   245	    fn apply(&self, source: &Self::Source, edits: &[Self::Edit]) -> Self::Source;
   246	
   247	    /// Incrementally recompile `source` under `edits` at `basis`.
   248	    ///
   249	    /// Must equal `self.full(&self.apply(source, edits), basis)` (v4 §112).
   250	    fn incremental(
   251	        &self,
   252	        source: &Self::Source,
   253	        edits: &[Self::Edit],
   254	        basis: &WorkspaceBasis,
   255	    ) -> Self::Output;
   256	}

   113	  schemas only. They may not share parser events, lowering code, canonicalizers,

    54	    fn full(&self, source: &Self::Source, _basis: &WorkspaceBasis) -> Self::Output {

    58	    fn apply(&self, source: &Self::Source, edits: &[Self::Edit]) -> Self::Source {
    59	        let mut output = source.clone();
    60	        let mut ordered = edits
    61	            .iter()
    62	            .filter_map(|edit| {
    63	                (edit.start <= edit.end
    64	                    && edit.end <= source.len()
    65	                    && source.is_char_boundary(edit.start)
    66	                    && source.is_char_boundary(edit.end))
    67	                .then_some((edit.start, edit.end, edit.replacement.as_str()))
    68	            })
    69	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    70	        ordered.sort_by(|left, right| right.0.cmp(&left.0).then(right.1.cmp(&left.1)));
    71	
    72	        for index in 0..ordered.len() {
    73	            let (start, end, replacement) = ordered[index];
    74	            // Edits use original-source offsets. Overlapping edits have no
    75	            // deterministic sequential meaning, so discard every member of
    76	            // an overlap set fail-closed.
    77	            let overlaps =
    78	                ordered
    79	                    .iter()
    80	                    .enumerate()
    81	                    .any(|(other, &(other_start, other_end, _))| {
    82	                        if other == index {
    83	                            return false;
    84	                        }
    85	                        // Empty edits are insertions at an original offset.
    86	                        // Two insertions at one offset, or an insertion on a
    87	                        // replacement boundary, have no deterministic order;
    88	                        // reject the whole overlap set fail-closed.
    89	                        if start == end && other_start == other_end {
    90	                            start == other_start
    91	                        } else if start == end {
    92	                            other_start <= start && start <= other_end
    93	                        } else if other_start == other_end {
    94	                            start <= other_start && other_start <= end
    95	                        } else {
    96	                            start < other_end && other_start < end
    97	                        }
    98	                    });
    99	            if overlaps {
   100	                continue;
   101	            }
   102	            output.replace_range(start..end, replacement);
   103	        }
   104	        output
   105	    }

   107	    fn incremental(

   109	        source: &Self::Source,
   110	        edits: &[Self::Edit],

   116	        let edited = self.apply(source, edits);

   122	/// Independently scan the tiny paragraph grammar used as the Phase 1
   123	/// incremental oracle. This intentionally does not call `paragraph::parse`.
   124	fn incremental_paragraph_oracle(input: &str) -> Vec<Block> {
   125	    let line_starts = std::iter::once(0)
   126	        .chain(input.match_indices('\n').map(|(offset, _)| offset + 1))
   127	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
   128	    let mut blocks = Vec::new();
   129	    let mut current_lines = Vec::new();
   130	    let mut block_start = None;
   131	    let mut block_end = 0;
   132	
   133	    for (line_index, line) in input.lines().enumerate() {
   134	        if line.trim().is_empty() {
   135	            if let Some(start) = block_start.take() {
   136	                blocks.push(build_oracle_block(&current_lines, start, block_end));
   137	                current_lines.clear();
   138	            }
   139	            continue;
   140	        }
   141	
   142	        let line_start = line_starts[line_index];
   143	        block_start.get_or_insert(line_start);
   144	        block_end = line_start + line.len();
   145	        current_lines.push(line);
   146	    }
   147	
   148	    if let Some(start) = block_start {
   149	        blocks.push(build_oracle_block(&current_lines, start, block_end));
   150	    }
   151	
   152	    blocks
   153	}
   154	
   155	fn build_oracle_block(lines: &[&str], start: usize, end: usize) -> Block {
   156	    let last_line = lines.last().expect("oracle blocks are non-empty");
   157	    let (id, cleaned_last_line) = extract_oracle_marker(last_line);
   158	    let mut text_lines = lines.to_vec();
   159	
   160	    if let Some(cleaned) = cleaned_last_line.as_deref() {
   161	        if cleaned.is_empty() {
   162	            text_lines.pop();
   163	        } else {
   164	            *text_lines.last_mut().expect("oracle blocks are non-empty") = cleaned;
   165	        }
   166	    }
   167	
   168	    Block {
   169	        text: text_lines.join("\n"),
   170	        id,
   171	        range: SourceRange {
   172	            start: start as u64,
   173	            end: end as u64,
   174	        },
   175	    }
   176	}
   177	
   178	/// Independently implement paragraph's terminal `{#id}` grammar.
   179	fn extract_oracle_marker(line: &str) -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {
   180	    let Some(marker_start) = line.rfind("{#") else {
   181	        return (None, None);
   182	    };
   183	    let marker = &line[marker_start + 2..];
   184	    let Some(close) = marker.find('}') else {
   185	        return (None, None);
   186	    };
   187	    let id = &marker[..close];
   188	
   189	    if id.is_empty()
   190	        || !id
   191	            .chars()
   192	            .all(|character| character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(character, '-' | '_'))
   193	        || !marker[close + 1..].trim().is_empty()
   194	    {
   195	        return (None, None);
   196	    }
   197	
   198	    let cleaned = line[..marker_start].trim_end().to_owned();
   199	    (Some(id.to_owned()), Some(cleaned))
   200	}

   202	/// A pure revisioned computation over a declared Workspace Basis (v4 §24).
   203	///
   204	/// SHAPE PROVISIONAL — this seam exists so §112 laws and the conformance
   205	/// harness compile as generics now; Phase -1.3/0 may reshape it freely.
   206	///
   207	/// Contract (v4 §24): results are deterministic for a declared basis and
   208	/// immutable once produced. Implementations must record every Basis component
   209	/// they read into `deps` — component-granular dependency tracking is what
   210	/// makes precise invalidation possible (v4 §7.5; R4 §10 "buffer generations
   211	/// invalidate only dependent queries"). Effects are forbidden inside
   212	/// `execute` (v4 §8.6, §118A).
   213	pub trait Query {
   214	    /// The immutable query result.
   215	    type Output;
   216	
   217	    /// Execute the query at `basis`, recording every component read into
   218	    /// `deps` (v4 §24 "dependency tracking", "precise invalidation").
   219	    fn execute(&self, basis: &WorkspaceBasis, deps: &mut ComponentDeps) -> Self::Output;
   220	}

   222	/// The incremental-equals-full compilation seam (v4 §112).
   223	///
   224	/// SHAPE PROVISIONAL — exists only so the §112 law compiles as a generic
   225	/// conformance test now; Phase -1.3/1 may reshape it freely.
   226	///
   227	/// Law (v4 §112): at the same Basis,
   228	/// `incremental(x, edits)` must equal `full(apply(x, edits))` —
   229	/// an incremental compile may never diverge from the from-scratch compile of
   230	/// the edited source. `Output: PartialEq` exists precisely so the law is
   231	/// checkable, and so unchanged results can stop invalidation cascades
   232	/// (v4 §24 "equality checks to prevent cascading unchanged results").
   233	pub trait IncrementalCompiler {
   234	    /// The source representation being compiled.
   235	    type Source;
   236	    /// One edit applicable to the source.
   237	    type Edit;
   238	    /// The compilation result; `PartialEq` so the §112 law is checkable.
   239	    type Output: PartialEq;
   240	
   241	    /// Compile `source` from scratch at `basis`.
   242	    fn full(&self, source: &Self::Source, basis: &WorkspaceBasis) -> Self::Output;
   243	
   244	    /// Apply `edits` to `source`, producing the edited source.
   245	    fn apply(&self, source: &Self::Source, edits: &[Self::Edit]) -> Self::Source;

   247	    /// Incrementally recompile `source` under `edits` at `basis`.

   249	    /// Must equal `self.full(&self.apply(source, edits), basis)` (v4 §112).
   250	    fn incremental(
   251	        &self,
   252	        source: &Self::Source,
   253	        edits: &[Self::Edit],
   254	        basis: &WorkspaceBasis,
   255	    ) -> Self::Output;
   256	}
