  2699	/// A reviewer cannot make its own "independent reproduction" true by setting
  2700	/// two booleans in one record. Every reproduced finding must have one matching
  2701	/// verified defect in the other isolated pass, with the same attack class,
  2702	/// exact source target, and identical falsification claim/observation. This
  2703	/// prevents two semantically different reports at one line from becoming a
  2704	/// concurrence by coordinate coincidence; finding IDs remain pass-local.
  2705	/// Whether two blinded passes are reporting the same defect. Blind pass 1 at
  2706	/// `0a0b4b4b` (A10): this required the `attempt` and `observed_result` strings
  2707	/// to be byte-identical. Two reviewers who cannot see each other's work will
  2708	/// not write the same sentence, so a genuine independent reproduction was
  2709	/// rejected unless they coordinated wording — which is the one thing the
  2710	/// blinding exists to prevent. The class and the coordinate already match by
  2711	/// the time this is asked; what is left to establish is that the two are about
  2712	/// the same thing, and shared vocabulary establishes it. Four significant
  2713	/// words in common is far more than coincidence at one coordinate and far less
  2714	/// than dictation.
  2715	fn reports_the_same_defect(
  2716	    left: &ReviewRecordAttempt,
  2717	    right: &ReviewRecordAttempt,
  2718	    corpus: &[&ReviewRecordAttempt],
  2719	    source_vocabulary: Option<&BTreeSet<String>>,
  2720	) -> bool {
  2721	    // Blind pass 1 at `ec045588` (A02): both reports name the coordinate, so
  2722	    // `crates`, `liminal`, `xtask` and `haq` were four shared words before
  2723	    // either said anything — the coordinate matched twice, once as itself and
  2724	    // once as vocabulary. Words the coordinate already carries are struck out,
  2725	    // and so are the handful this campaign puts in every report.
  2726	    const UBIQUITOUS: [&str; 8] = [
  2727	        "verifier",
  2728	        "verify",
  2729	        "packet",
  2730	        "evidence",
  2731	        "check",
  2732	        "checks",
  2733	        "because",
  2734	        "committed",
  2735	    ];
  2736	    let coordinate: BTreeSet<String> = format!("{} {}", left.target, right.target)
  2737	        .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2738	        .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')
  2739	        .map(str::to_owned)
  2740	        .collect();
  2741	    let vocabulary = |attempt: &ReviewRecordAttempt| {
  2742	        format!("{} {}", attempt.attempt, attempt.observed_result)
  2743	            .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2744	            .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')
  2745	            .filter(|word| word.len() >= 4)
  2746	            .filter(|word| !coordinate.contains(*word))
  2747	            .filter(|word| !UBIQUITOUS.contains(word))
  2748	            .map(str::to_owned)
  2749	            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
  2750	    };
  2751	    let shared: BTreeSet<String> = vocabulary(left)
  2752	        .intersection(&vocabulary(right))
  2753	        .cloned()
  2754	        .collect();
  2755	    if shared.len() < 4 {
  2756	        return false;
  2757	    }
  2758	    // Blind pass 1 at `2bba9071` (A09): four shared words is a count, and a
  2759	    // count is satisfied by four words this campaign puts in every report.
  2760	    // What makes two reports the same report is sharing something RARE — a
  2761	    // word that does not appear all over the rest of the record. Two such
  2762	    // words, measured against every attempt in both passes rather than
  2763	    // against a list someone maintains.
  2764	    let distinctive = shared
  2765	        .iter()
  2766	        .filter(|word| {
  2767	            // Shared prose is only a concurrence signal when it also names
  2768	            // vocabulary present in the cited source. This blocks unrelated
  2769	            // reports manufactured from four private nonce words while still
  2770	            // allowing independently worded descriptions of real code.
  2771	            source_vocabulary.is_none_or(|source| source.contains(word.as_str()))
  2772	        })
  2773	        .filter(|word| {
  2774	            corpus
  2775	                .iter()
  2776	                .filter(|attempt| {
  2777	                    format!("{} {}", attempt.attempt, attempt.observed_result)
  2778	                        .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2779	                        .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')
  2780	                        .any(|token| token == word.as_str())
  2781	                })
  2782	                .count()
  2783	                <= 2
  2784	        })
  2785	        .count();
  2786	    distinctive >= 2
  2787	}

  2966	/// `redact_evidence` from `scripts/haqp_blind_review.py`, which substitutes
  2967	/// `****` for each match of its `CREDENTIAL_SHAPED` pattern:
  2968	///
  2969	/// - a known vendor prefix followed by 12 or more of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, or
  2970	/// - a run of 24 or more of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` holding a lowercase letter, an
  2971	///   uppercase letter and a digit.
  2972	///

  2974	/// as `re.sub` does. The second alternative looks ahead over the whole run
  2975	/// from its start, so a run that fails it has no suffix that passes.
  2976	fn redact_evidence(text: &str) -> String {
  2977	    const PREFIXES: [&str; 10] = [
  2978	        "sk-", "AIza", "ghp_", "gho_", "xoxb-", "xoxa-", "xoxp-", "xoxr-", "xoxs-", "hf_",
  2979	    ];
  2980	    let is_key_byte = |b: u8| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'_' || b == b'-';
  2981	    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
  2982	    let run_from = |at: usize| bytes[at..].iter().take_while(|b| is_key_byte(**b)).count();
  2983	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
  2984	    let mut at = 0;
  2985	    while at < bytes.len() {
  2986	        let rest = &text[at..];
  2987	        let prefixed = PREFIXES.iter().find_map(|prefix| {
  2988	            if !rest.starts_with(prefix) {
  2989	                return None;
  2990	            }
  2991	            let tail = run_from(at + prefix.len());
  2992	            (tail >= 12).then_some(prefix.len() + tail)
  2993	        });
  2994	        let shaped = || {
  2995	            let run = &bytes[at..at + run_from(at)];
  2996	            (run.len() >= 24
  2997	                && run.iter().any(u8::is_ascii_lowercase)
  2998	                && run.iter().any(u8::is_ascii_uppercase)
  2999	                && run.iter().any(u8::is_ascii_digit))
  3000	            .then_some(run.len())
  3001	        };
  3002	        if let Some(len) = prefixed.or_else(shaped) {
  3003	            out.push_str("****");
  3004	            at += len;
  3005	        } else {
  3006	            let ch = rest
  3007	                .chars()
  3008	                .next()
  3009	                .expect("at is a char boundary below len");
  3010	            out.push(ch);
  3011	            at += ch.len_utf8();
  3012	        }
  3013	    }
  3014	    out
  3015	}

  3019	/// answer).
  3020	/// A standing ruling on a class of reviewer finding (grilling decision 6,
  3021	/// 2026-09-03): a finding Brian rules incorrect is cleared by a ruling
  3022	/// commit signed against the pinned signer, never by editing the record.
  3023	/// Rulings live in `docs/execution/rulings/*.md` with a front matter of
  3024	/// `id`, `attack_class`, `target` (a repository path) and `status`
  3025	/// (`draft` or `ruled`). A ruling cannot name its own commit, so the commit
  3026	/// that counts is the last one that touched the ruling's file.
  3027	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]

  3029	    id: String,
  3030	    attack_class: String,
  3031	    target: String,
  3032	    /// Phrases that must all appear in an attempt's prose for this ruling to
  3033	    /// answer it. Blind pass 1 at aa00d41 (A08): matching on class and file
  3034	    /// alone cleared an unrelated second claim in the same class and file —
  3035	    /// R-001, written for "stage reads are leakage", silently cleared a
  3036	    /// genuine untracked-chdir defect. A ruling answers a claim, not a
  3037	    /// coordinate.

  3039	    /// Phrases whose presence means this ruling does NOT answer the claim.
  3040	    /// Blind pass 1 at 5fb1b57 (A08): a required phrase can be found inside a
  3041	    /// sentence that negates it, so a ruling could suppress a defect it was
  3042	    /// never shown. Required phrases say what a claim must be about;
  3043	    /// excluded ones say what it must not be about.
  3044	    claim_excludes: Vec<String>,
  3045	    status: String,
  3046	    file: String,
  3047	}

  3049	const RULING_SIGNERS: &str = "conformance/haqp/ruling-signers";

  3051	fn rulings(root: &Utf8Path) -> Result<Vec<Ruling>> {
  3052	    let dir = root.join("docs/execution/rulings");
  3053	    if !dir.is_dir() {
  3054	        return Ok(Vec::new());
  3055	    }
  3056	    let mut files = fs::read_dir(dir.as_std_path())?
  3057	        .map(|entry| entry.map(|e| e.path()))
  3058	        .collect::<std::io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
  3059	    files.sort();
  3060	    let mut out = Vec::new();
  3061	    for file in files {
  3062	        let file = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(file)
  3063	            .map_err(|p| anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path {}", p.display()))?;
  3064	        if file.extension() != Some("md") {
  3065	            continue;
  3066	        }
  3067	        let text = fs::read_to_string(&file)?;
  3068	        let front = text
  3069	            .strip_prefix("---\n")
  3070	            .and_then(|rest| rest.split_once("\n---\n"))
  3071	            .map(|(front, _)| front)
  3072	            .with_context(|| format!("{file}: ruling has no front matter"))?;
  3073	        let field = |key: &str| -> Result<String> {
  3074	            front
  3075	                .lines()
  3076	                .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix(&format!("{key}: ")))
  3077	                .map(|v| v.trim().trim_matches('"').to_owned())
  3078	                .with_context(|| format!("{file}: ruling front matter lacks {key}"))
  3079	        };
  3080	        let excludes = field("claim_excludes").unwrap_or_default();
  3081	        let requires = field("claim_requires")?;
  3082	        anyhow::ensure!(
  3083	            !requires.trim().is_empty(),
  3084	            "{file}: ruling claim_requires is empty; a ruling that answers any claim in its \
  3085	             class and file clears defects it was never shown (A08)"
  3086	        );
  3087	        out.push(Ruling {
  3088	            id: field("id")?,
  3089	            attack_class: field("attack_class")?,
  3090	            target: field("target")?,
  3091	            claim_requires: requires
  3092	                .split(';')
  3093	                .map(|phrase| phrase.trim().to_ascii_lowercase())
  3094	                .filter(|phrase| !phrase.is_empty())
  3095	                .collect(),
  3096	            claim_excludes: excludes
  3097	                .split(';')
  3098	                .map(|phrase| phrase.trim().to_ascii_lowercase())
  3099	                .filter(|phrase| !phrase.is_empty())
  3100	                .collect(),
  3101	            status: field("status")?,
  3102	            file: file.strip_prefix(root).unwrap_or(&file).to_string(),
  3103	        });
  3104	    }
  3105	    Ok(out)
  3106	}

  3108	/// A ruling is in force when its status is `ruled` and the last commit that
  3109	/// touched its file verifies against the pinned signers. A draft, an
  3110	/// uncommitted edit, or an unsigned commit clears nothing.
  3111	fn ruling_in_force(root: &Utf8Path, ruling: &Ruling) -> Result<bool> {
  3112	    if ruling.status != "ruled" {
  3113	        return Ok(false);
  3114	    }
  3115	    let signers = root.join(RULING_SIGNERS);
  3116	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3117	        signers.is_file(),
  3118	        "{RULING_SIGNERS} is missing; a ruling cannot be verified against no signer"
  3119	    );
  3120	    let dirty = git_text(root, &["status", "--porcelain", "--", &ruling.file])?;
  3121	    if !dirty.trim().is_empty() {
  3122	        return Ok(false);
  3123	    }
  3124	    let commit = git_text(root, &["log", "-1", "--format=%H", "--", &ruling.file])?;
  3125	    if commit.trim().is_empty() {
  3126	        return Ok(false);
  3127	    }
  3128	    let verified = Command::new("git")
  3129	        .current_dir(root)
  3130	        .args(["-c", "gpg.format=ssh", "-c"])
  3131	        .arg(format!("gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile={signers}"))
  3132	        .args(["verify-commit", commit.trim()])
  3133	        .output()
  3134	        .context("git verify-commit")?;
  3135	    Ok(verified.status.success())
  3136	}

  3138	/// The findings a record leaves unresolved after standing rulings: verified,
  3139	/// independently reproduced, not resolved by a fix proof, and not covered by
  3140	/// a ruling in force on the same attack class and target file. Read as plain
  3141	/// JSON so the count is over what was persisted.
  3142	pub fn effective_unresolved_findings_repo(root: &Utf8Path, record: &Utf8Path) -> Result<u64> {
  3143	    let value: serde_json::Value =
  3144	        serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(record)?).with_context(|| format!("parse {record}"))?;
  3145	    let in_force = rulings(root)?
  3146	        .into_iter()
  3147	        .filter(|ruling| ruling_in_force(root, ruling).unwrap_or(false))
  3148	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  3149	    effective_unresolved_findings(&in_force, &value, record)
  3150	}

  3152	/// The count, given the rulings already established to be in force. Split from
  3153	/// the repository walk so the clearance rules can be exercised without a
  3154	/// signing key: a rule the tests cannot reach is a rule nothing checks.
  3155	fn effective_unresolved_findings(
  3156	    in_force: &[Ruling],
  3157	    value: &serde_json::Value,
  3158	    record: &Utf8Path,
  3159	) -> Result<u64> {
  3160	    // Counted from each attempt's own flags, not through the findings list:
  3161	    // a verified, reproduced attempt the reviewer forgot to list as a finding
  3162	    // is still unresolved.
  3163	    let mut unresolved = 0u64;
  3164	    let mut cleared: BTreeMap<String, u64> = BTreeMap::new();
  3165	    for attempt in value["attempts"].as_array().into_iter().flatten() {
  3166	        let class = attempt["attack_class"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
  3167	        let target = attempt["target"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
  3168	        if attempt["classification"].as_str() != Some("verified_defect")
  3169	            || !attempt["independently_reproduced"]
  3170	                .as_bool()
  3171	                .unwrap_or(false)
  3172	            || attempt["resolved"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false)
  3173	        {
  3174	            continue;
  3175	        }
  3176	        let target_file = target.split(':').next().unwrap_or(target);
  3177	        let prose = format!(
  3178	            "{} {}",
  3179	            attempt["attempt"].as_str().unwrap_or_default(),
  3180	            attempt["observed_result"].as_str().unwrap_or_default()
  3181	        )
  3182	        .to_ascii_lowercase();
  3183	        // Blind pass 1 at c29bc0ea (A08): a ruling matched on class, file and
  3184	        // prose substrings, so an unrelated defect in the same file whose
  3185	        // wording happened to carry the required phrases was cleared in
  3186	        // silence. Two things changed. A ruling that names a coordinate is
  3187	        // held to it, not merely to the file. And a ruling clears at most one
  3188	        // attempt per record: matching a second is evidence the phrases are
  3189	        // too broad, and the answer to that is a refusal, not two clearances.
  3190	        let matched = in_force
  3191	            .iter()
  3192	            .filter(|ruling| {
  3193	                ruling.attack_class == class
  3194	                    && if ruling.target.contains(':') {
  3195	                        ruling.target == target
  3196	                    } else {
  3197	                        ruling.target == target_file
  3198	                    }
  3199	                    && ruling
  3200	                        .claim_requires
  3201	                        .iter()
  3202	                        .all(|phrase| prose.contains(phrase.as_str()))
  3203	                    && !ruling
  3204	                        .claim_excludes
  3205	                        .iter()
  3206	                        .any(|phrase| prose.contains(phrase.as_str()))
  3207	            })
  3208	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  3209	        for ruling in &matched {
  3210	            *cleared.entry(ruling.id.clone()).or_insert(0u64) += 1;
  3211	        }
  3212	        if matched.is_empty() {
  3213	            unresolved += 1;
  3214	        }
  3215	    }
  3216	    for (id, count) in &cleared {
  3217	        anyhow::ensure!(
  3218	            *count <= 1,
  3219	            "ruling {id} cleared {count} separate findings in {record}; a ruling \
  3220	                 answers one claim, so phrases matching more than one are too \
  3221	                 broad to stand"
  3222	        );
  3223	    }
  3224	    Ok(unresolved)
  3225	}

  3227	/// The receipt must be the backend's own shape, and a Codex transcript must be
  3228	/// retained beside the record and hash to what the receipt claims (F-49).
  3229	/// The last assistant message in a codex rollout: what the provider actually
  3230	/// said, as its own transcript records it.
  3231	fn transcript_final_message(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {

  3234	        let Ok(record) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(line) else {

  3239	            || payload["type"] != "message"
  3240	            || payload["role"] != "assistant"
  3241	        {
  3242	            continue;
  3243	        }

  3245	            .as_array()?
  3246	            .iter()
  3247	            .filter_map(|part| part["text"].as_str())
  3248	            .collect::<String>();
  3249	        spoken = Some(text);
  3250	    }
  3251	    spoken
  3252	}

  3254	/// A codex receipt: the session it names, the transcript it retained, and
  3255	/// that the answer beside the record is the one the transcript records the
  3256	/// provider giving.
  3257	fn verify_codex_receipt(record: &ReviewRecord, record_path: &Utf8Path) -> Result<()> {
  3258	    let receipt = &record.provider_receipt;
  3259	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3260	        !receipt.session_id.trim().is_empty() && !receipt.session_file.trim().is_empty(),
  3261	        "a codex receipt must name the session that answered"
  3262	    );
  3263	    require_hex_digest("review transcript_sha256", &receipt.transcript_sha256)?;
  3264	    let transcript = record_path.with_extension("session.jsonl");
  3265	    let bytes = fs::read(&transcript).with_context(|| {
  3266	        format!("{transcript}: the codex transcript must be retained beside its record")
  3267	    })?;
  3268	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3269	        bytes.len() as u64 == receipt.transcript_bytes,
  3270	        "codex transcript is {} bytes, receipt claims {}",
  3271	        bytes.len(),
  3272	        receipt.transcript_bytes
  3273	    );
  3274	    require_eq(
  3275	        "review transcript_sha256 (of the retained transcript)",
  3276	        &format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(&bytes)),
  3277	        &receipt.transcript_sha256,
  3278	    )?;
  3279	    // Blind pass 1 at `aeed70f9` (A09): the transcript's bytes were
  3280	    // authenticated and its IDENTITY was not — `session_id` and
  3281	    // `session_file` only had to be non-empty, so a record could name
  3282	    // one session and retain another's rollout. A rollout opens with
  3283	    // its own `session_meta`, and the receipt's id ends with the UUID
  3284	    // that record carries.
  3285	    let first = std::str::from_utf8(&bytes)
  3286	        .context("codex transcript is not UTF-8")?
  3287	        .lines()
  3288	        .next()
  3289	        .context("codex transcript is empty")?;
  3290	    let meta: serde_json::Value =
  3291	        serde_json::from_str(first).context("codex transcript's first record is not JSON")?;
  3292	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3293	        meta["type"] == "session_meta",
  3294	        "a codex rollout opens with session_meta; this one opens with {:?}",
  3295	        meta["type"]
  3296	    );
  3297	    let declared = meta["payload"]["session_id"]
  3298	        .as_str()
  3299	        .context("codex session_meta carries no session_id")?;
  3300	    // Codex names a rollout `<timestamp>-<uuid>` and its `session_meta`
  3301	    // carries the bare uuid, so the receipt's id either IS the declared
  3302	    // id or ends with it after a separator. Review of `bba803d4`: a
  3303	    // bare `ends_with` would also accept `xfixture` for `fixture`,
  3304	    // which is a different session.
  3305	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3306	        receipt.session_id == declared || receipt.session_id.ends_with(&format!("-{declared}")),
  3307	        "receipt names session {:?}, retained transcript is session {declared:?}",
  3308	        receipt.session_id
  3309	    );
  3310	    require_eq(
  3311	        "review provider_receipt session_file",
  3312	        &receipt.session_file,
  3313	        &format!("rollout-{}.jsonl", receipt.session_id),
  3314	    )?;
  3315	    // Blind pass 1 at `3720d179` (A09): the raw answer and the
  3316	    // transcript were each hashed and neither was checked against the
  3317	    // other, so a record could retain a real session and a different
  3318	    // answer — both digests true, the pair a fiction. The rollout's
  3319	    // last assistant message IS the answer the runner saved.
  3320	    let raw_path = record_path.with_extension("raw.txt");
  3321	    let raw = fs::read_to_string(&raw_path)
  3322	        .with_context(|| format!("{raw_path}: the raw answer must be retained"))?;
  3323	    let spoken = transcript_final_message(&bytes)
  3324	        .with_context(|| format!("{transcript}: the transcript carries no assistant message"))?;
  3325	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3326	        spoken.trim() == raw.trim(),
  3327	        "the retained answer is not the one the transcript records the provider giving"
  3328	    );
  3329	    Ok(())
  3330	}

  3358	                    .contains(record.reviewer.model_family.as_str())
  3359	                    || record
  3360	                        .reviewer
  3361	                        .model_family
  3362	                        .contains(receipt.provider_model.as_str()),

  3364	                receipt.provider_model,

  3366	            );
  3367	            anyhow::ensure!(

  3420	/// The commands a resolution receipt may claim, and the gate RUNS the one it
  3421	/// claims (A09/A10 at 9eca4f0).
  3422	///
  3423	/// Before this, a receipt naming any command with a self-authored
  3424	/// `verification_exit_code: 0` was accepted without the command ever being
  3425	/// executed — the resolution asserted its own success. The command is drawn
  3426	/// from a closed registry rather than run as written: executing arbitrary text
  3427	/// out of an evidence file would hand whoever wrote the file this process.
  3428	const RESOLUTION_COMMANDS: [(&str, &[&str]); 4] = [
  3429	    ("just ci", &["just", "ci"]),
  3430	    ("just haq-inventory", &["just", "haq-inventory"]),
  3431	    ("just haq-canaries", &["just", "haq-canaries"]),
  3432	    (
  3433	        "cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features",
  3434	        &["cargo", "nextest", "run", "--workspace", "--all-features"],

  3437	
  3438	/// The registry's commands are the project's own gates, run with the gate's
  3439	/// environment and no timeout: they are what CI runs, so a hang here is a hang
  3440	/// in CI, visible either way (review of `e490671`). The working directory is a
  3441	/// disposable worktree at the commit the receipt names, never the live tree.
  3442	fn verify_resolution_command_ran(
  3443	    root: &Utf8Path,
  3444	    who: &str,
  3445	    evidence_text: &str,
  3446	    commit: &str,
  3447	) -> Result<()> {
  3448	    let claimed = evidence_text
  3449	        .lines()
  3450	        .find_map(|line| line.trim_start().strip_prefix("verification_command:"))
  3451	        .map(str::trim)
  3452	        .unwrap_or_default();
  3453	    let argv = RESOLUTION_COMMANDS
  3454	        .iter()
  3455	        .find(|(name, _)| *name == claimed)
  3456	        .map(|(_, argv)| *argv)
  3457	        .with_context(|| {
  3458	            format!(
  3459	                "{who}: resolution claims verification command {claimed:?}, which is not one the \
  3460	                 gate can run; the registry is closed so a receipt cannot name a command that \
  3461	                 exists only in its own text"

  2596	/// `verify_generated_inventory` treats seeds and evidence hashes.

  2602	            .independently_reproduced
  2603	            .iter()
  2604	            .filter(|id| !raised.contains(id))

  2608	                "{} claims to have independently reproduced {unverified:?}, which it \
  2609	                 never raised as findings",
  2610	                review.reviewer

  2614	        // independent reproduction; otherwise "verified" means one model said so.

  2629	            anyhow::bail!(
  2630	                "{} claims pass with no committed record; the lane's own output lives \
  2631	                 under target/ and cannot be read back",
  2632	                review.reviewer
  2633	            );

  2636	        // paths are not taken on faith. `join` DISCARDS the base when handed an
  2637	        // absolute path, so `evidence: "/etc/passwd"` would read straight out of
  2638	        // the repository; `..` walks out just as effectively.

  2641	            || candidate
  2642	                .components()
  2643	                .any(|part| part == camino::Utf8Component::ParentDir)

  2645	            anyhow::bail!(
  2646	                "{} points its record at {evidence:?}, which escapes the repository; \
  2647	                 evidence paths must be relative and contain no `..`",
  2648	                review.reviewer
  2649	            );

  2653	            .context("canonicalize repository root for review evidence")?;

  2655	            format!(
  2656	                "{path}: {} claims pass but its record is missing",
  2657	                review.reviewer
  2658	            )
  2659	        })?;

  2661	            canonical_path.starts_with(&canonical_root),
  2662	            "{} review record resolves outside repository via symlink",
  2663	            review.reviewer
  2664	        );

  2666	            format!(
  2667	                "{path}: {} claims pass but its record is missing",
  2668	                review.reviewer
  2669	            )
  2670	        })?;

  2672	            serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).with_context(|| format!("parse {path}"))?;

  2675	            .provenance
  2676	            .as_ref()
  2677	            .context("qualified review evidence requires packet provenance")?;

  2679	            "review record fixed_base.commit",
  2680	            &record.fixed_base.commit,
  2681	            &provenance.fixed_commit,
  2682	        )?;

  2684	            "review record fixed_base.tree",
  2685	            &record.fixed_base.tree,

  2689	            record.fixed_base.clean,
  2690	            "{} review record was produced from a dirty fixed base",
  2691	            review.reviewer
  2692	        );

  2699	/// A reviewer cannot make its own "independent reproduction" true by setting
  2700	/// two booleans in one record. Every reproduced finding must have one matching
  2701	/// verified defect in the other isolated pass, with the same attack class,
  2702	/// exact source target, and identical falsification claim/observation. This
  2703	/// prevents two semantically different reports at one line from becoming a
  2704	/// concurrence by coordinate coincidence; finding IDs remain pass-local.
  2705	/// Whether two blinded passes are reporting the same defect. Blind pass 1 at
  2706	/// `0a0b4b4b` (A10): this required the `attempt` and `observed_result` strings
  2707	/// to be byte-identical. Two reviewers who cannot see each other's work will
  2708	/// not write the same sentence, so a genuine independent reproduction was
  2709	/// rejected unless they coordinated wording — which is the one thing the
  2710	/// blinding exists to prevent. The class and the coordinate already match by
  2711	/// the time this is asked; what is left to establish is that the two are about
  2712	/// the same thing, and shared vocabulary establishes it. Four significant
  2713	/// words in common is far more than coincidence at one coordinate and far less
  2714	/// than dictation.
  2715	fn reports_the_same_defect(
  2716	    left: &ReviewRecordAttempt,
  2717	    right: &ReviewRecordAttempt,
  2718	    corpus: &[&ReviewRecordAttempt],
  2719	    source_vocabulary: Option<&BTreeSet<String>>,
  2720	) -> bool {
  2721	    // Blind pass 1 at `ec045588` (A02): both reports name the coordinate, so
  2722	    // `crates`, `liminal`, `xtask` and `haq` were four shared words before
  2723	    // either said anything — the coordinate matched twice, once as itself and
  2724	    // once as vocabulary. Words the coordinate already carries are struck out,
  2725	    // and so are the handful this campaign puts in every report.
  2726	    const UBIQUITOUS: [&str; 8] = [
  2727	        "verifier",
  2728	        "verify",
  2729	        "packet",
  2730	        "evidence",
  2731	        "check",
  2732	        "checks",
  2733	        "because",
  2734	        "committed",
  2735	    ];
  2736	    let coordinate: BTreeSet<String> = format!("{} {}", left.target, right.target)
  2737	        .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2738	        .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')
  2739	        .map(str::to_owned)
  2740	        .collect();
  2741	    let vocabulary = |attempt: &ReviewRecordAttempt| {
  2742	        format!("{} {}", attempt.attempt, attempt.observed_result)
  2743	            .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2744	            .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')
  2745	            .filter(|word| word.len() >= 4)
  2746	            .filter(|word| !coordinate.contains(*word))
  2747	            .filter(|word| !UBIQUITOUS.contains(word))
  2748	            .map(str::to_owned)
  2749	            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
  2750	    };
  2751	    let shared: BTreeSet<String> = vocabulary(left)
  2752	        .intersection(&vocabulary(right))
  2753	        .cloned()
  2754	        .collect();
  2755	    if shared.len() < 4 {
  2756	        return false;
  2757	    }
  2758	    // Blind pass 1 at `2bba9071` (A09): four shared words is a count, and a
  2759	    // count is satisfied by four words this campaign puts in every report.
  2760	    // What makes two reports the same report is sharing something RARE — a
  2761	    // word that does not appear all over the rest of the record. Two such
  2762	    // words, measured against every attempt in both passes rather than
  2763	    // against a list someone maintains.
  2764	    let distinctive = shared
  2765	        .iter()
  2766	        .filter(|word| {
  2767	            // Shared prose is only a concurrence signal when it also names
  2768	            // vocabulary present in the cited source. This blocks unrelated
  2769	            // reports manufactured from four private nonce words while still
  2770	            // allowing independently worded descriptions of real code.
  2771	            source_vocabulary.is_none_or(|source| source.contains(word.as_str()))
  2772	        })
  2773	        .filter(|word| {
  2774	            corpus
  2775	                .iter()
  2776	                .filter(|attempt| {
  2777	                    format!("{} {}", attempt.attempt, attempt.observed_result)
  2778	                        .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2779	                        .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')
  2780	                        .any(|token| token == word.as_str())
  2781	                })
  2782	                .count()
  2783	                <= 2
  2784	        })
  2785	        .count();
  2786	    distinctive >= 2
  2787	}

  2789	fn source_vocabulary(root: &Utf8Path, target: &str) -> Result<BTreeSet<String>> {
  2790	    let file = target
  2791	        .split(':')
  2792	        .next()
  2793	        .filter(|file| !file.trim().is_empty())
  2794	        .context("review target has no source file")?;
  2795	    // Resolve through the same repository-bound path guard used by every other
  2796	    // review artifact. A missing or escaping target must fail closed; treating
  2797	    // it as `None` would silently disable source-grounded concurrence.
  2798	    let path = safe_repo_path(root, file, "review target")?;
  2799	    let text = fs::read_to_string(&path).with_context(|| format!("read review target {path}"))?;
  2800	    Ok(text
  2801	        .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2802	        .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')
  2803	        .filter(|word| word.len() >= 4)
  2804	        .map(str::to_owned)
  2805	        .collect())
  2806	}

  2966	/// `redact_evidence` from `scripts/haqp_blind_review.py`, which substitutes
  2967	/// `****` for each match of its `CREDENTIAL_SHAPED` pattern:
  2968	///
  2969	/// - a known vendor prefix followed by 12 or more of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, or
  2970	/// - a run of 24 or more of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` holding a lowercase letter, an
  2971	///   uppercase letter and a digit.
  2972	///
  2973	/// Both alternatives consume greedily and matching resumes after each match,
  2974	/// as `re.sub` does. The second alternative looks ahead over the whole run
  2975	/// from its start, so a run that fails it has no suffix that passes.
  2976	fn redact_evidence(text: &str) -> String {
  2977	    const PREFIXES: [&str; 10] = [
  2978	        "sk-", "AIza", "ghp_", "gho_", "xoxb-", "xoxa-", "xoxp-", "xoxr-", "xoxs-", "hf_",
  2979	    ];
  2980	    let is_key_byte = |b: u8| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'_' || b == b'-';
  2981	    let bytes = text.as_bytes();
  2982	    let run_from = |at: usize| bytes[at..].iter().take_while(|b| is_key_byte(**b)).count();
  2983	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
  2984	    let mut at = 0;
  2985	    while at < bytes.len() {
  2986	        let rest = &text[at..];
  2987	        let prefixed = PREFIXES.iter().find_map(|prefix| {
  2988	            if !rest.starts_with(prefix) {
  2989	                return None;
  2990	            }
  2991	            let tail = run_from(at + prefix.len());
  2992	            (tail >= 12).then_some(prefix.len() + tail)
  2993	        });
  2994	        let shaped = || {
  2995	            let run = &bytes[at..at + run_from(at)];
  2996	            (run.len() >= 24
  2997	                && run.iter().any(u8::is_ascii_lowercase)
  2998	                && run.iter().any(u8::is_ascii_uppercase)
  2999	                && run.iter().any(u8::is_ascii_digit))
  3000	            .then_some(run.len())
  3001	        };
  3002	        if let Some(len) = prefixed.or_else(shaped) {
  3003	            out.push_str("****");
  3004	            at += len;
  3005	        } else {
  3006	            let ch = rest
  3007	                .chars()
  3008	                .next()
  3009	                .expect("at is a char boundary below len");
  3010	            out.push(ch);
  3011	            at += ch.len_utf8();
  3012	        }
  3013	    }
  3014	    out
  3015	}

  3051	fn rulings(root: &Utf8Path) -> Result<Vec<Ruling>> {

  3057	        .map(|entry| entry.map(|e| e.path()))
  3058	        .collect::<std::io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
  3059	    files.sort();
  3060	    let mut out = Vec::new();
  3061	    for file in files {
  3062	        let file = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(file)
  3063	            .map_err(|p| anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path {}", p.display()))?;
  3064	        if file.extension() != Some("md") {
  3065	            continue;
  3066	        }
  3067	        let text = fs::read_to_string(&file)?;
  3068	        let front = text
  3069	            .strip_prefix("---\n")
  3070	            .and_then(|rest| rest.split_once("\n---\n"))
  3071	            .map(|(front, _)| front)
  3072	            .with_context(|| format!("{file}: ruling has no front matter"))?;
  3073	        let field = |key: &str| -> Result<String> {
  3074	            front
  3075	                .lines()
  3076	                .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix(&format!("{key}: ")))
  3077	                .map(|v| v.trim().trim_matches('"').to_owned())
  3078	                .with_context(|| format!("{file}: ruling front matter lacks {key}"))
  3079	        };
  3080	        let excludes = field("claim_excludes").unwrap_or_default();
  3081	        let requires = field("claim_requires")?;
  3082	        anyhow::ensure!(
  3083	            !requires.trim().is_empty(),
  3084	            "{file}: ruling claim_requires is empty; a ruling that answers any claim in its \
  3085	             class and file clears defects it was never shown (A08)"
  3086	        );
  3087	        out.push(Ruling {
  3088	            id: field("id")?,
  3089	            attack_class: field("attack_class")?,
  3090	            target: field("target")?,
  3091	            claim_requires: requires
  3092	                .split(';')
  3093	                .map(|phrase| phrase.trim().to_ascii_lowercase())
  3094	                .filter(|phrase| !phrase.is_empty())
  3095	                .collect(),
  3096	            claim_excludes: excludes
  3097	                .split(';')
  3098	                .map(|phrase| phrase.trim().to_ascii_lowercase())
  3099	                .filter(|phrase| !phrase.is_empty())
  3100	                .collect(),
  3101	            status: field("status")?,
  3102	            file: file.strip_prefix(root).unwrap_or(&file).to_string(),
  3103	        });
  3104	    }
  3105	    Ok(out)
  3106	}

  3108	/// A ruling is in force when its status is `ruled` and the last commit that
  3109	/// touched its file verifies against the pinned signers. A draft, an
  3110	/// uncommitted edit, or an unsigned commit clears nothing.
  3111	fn ruling_in_force(root: &Utf8Path, ruling: &Ruling) -> Result<bool> {
  3112	    if ruling.status != "ruled" {
  3113	        return Ok(false);
  3114	    }
  3115	    let signers = root.join(RULING_SIGNERS);
  3116	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3117	        signers.is_file(),
  3118	        "{RULING_SIGNERS} is missing; a ruling cannot be verified against no signer"
  3119	    );
  3120	    let dirty = git_text(root, &["status", "--porcelain", "--", &ruling.file])?;
  3121	    if !dirty.trim().is_empty() {
  3122	        return Ok(false);
  3123	    }
  3124	    let commit = git_text(root, &["log", "-1", "--format=%H", "--", &ruling.file])?;
  3125	    if commit.trim().is_empty() {
  3126	        return Ok(false);
  3127	    }
  3128	    let verified = Command::new("git")
  3129	        .current_dir(root)
  3130	        .args(["-c", "gpg.format=ssh", "-c"])
  3131	        .arg(format!("gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile={signers}"))
  3132	        .args(["verify-commit", commit.trim()])
  3133	        .output()
  3134	        .context("git verify-commit")?;
  3135	    Ok(verified.status.success())
  3136	}

  3139	/// independently reproduced, not resolved by a fix proof, and not covered by
  3140	/// a ruling in force on the same attack class and target file. Read as plain
  3141	/// JSON so the count is over what was persisted.
  3142	pub fn effective_unresolved_findings_repo(root: &Utf8Path, record: &Utf8Path) -> Result<u64> {
  3143	    let value: serde_json::Value =
  3144	        serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(record)?).with_context(|| format!("parse {record}"))?;
  3145	    let in_force = rulings(root)?
  3146	        .into_iter()
  3147	        .filter(|ruling| ruling_in_force(root, ruling).unwrap_or(false))
  3148	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();

  3152	/// The count, given the rulings already established to be in force. Split from
  3153	/// the repository walk so the clearance rules can be exercised without a
  3154	/// signing key: a rule the tests cannot reach is a rule nothing checks.
  3155	fn effective_unresolved_findings(
  3156	    in_force: &[Ruling],
  3157	    value: &serde_json::Value,
  3158	    record: &Utf8Path,
  3159	) -> Result<u64> {
  3160	    // Counted from each attempt's own flags, not through the findings list:
  3161	    // a verified, reproduced attempt the reviewer forgot to list as a finding
  3162	    // is still unresolved.
  3163	    let mut unresolved = 0u64;
  3164	    let mut cleared: BTreeMap<String, u64> = BTreeMap::new();
  3165	    for attempt in value["attempts"].as_array().into_iter().flatten() {
  3166	        let class = attempt["attack_class"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
  3167	        let target = attempt["target"].as_str().unwrap_or_default();
  3168	        if attempt["classification"].as_str() != Some("verified_defect")
  3169	            || !attempt["independently_reproduced"]
  3170	                .as_bool()
  3171	                .unwrap_or(false)
  3172	            || attempt["resolved"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false)
  3173	        {
  3174	            continue;
  3175	        }
  3176	        let target_file = target.split(':').next().unwrap_or(target);
  3177	        let prose = format!(
  3178	            "{} {}",
  3179	            attempt["attempt"].as_str().unwrap_or_default(),
  3180	            attempt["observed_result"].as_str().unwrap_or_default()
  3181	        )
  3182	        .to_ascii_lowercase();
  3183	        // Blind pass 1 at c29bc0ea (A08): a ruling matched on class, file and
  3184	        // prose substrings, so an unrelated defect in the same file whose
  3185	        // wording happened to carry the required phrases was cleared in
  3186	        // silence. Two things changed. A ruling that names a coordinate is
  3187	        // held to it, not merely to the file. And a ruling clears at most one
  3188	        // attempt per record: matching a second is evidence the phrases are
  3189	        // too broad, and the answer to that is a refusal, not two clearances.
  3190	        let matched = in_force
  3191	            .iter()
  3192	            .filter(|ruling| {
  3193	                ruling.attack_class == class
  3194	                    && if ruling.target.contains(':') {
  3195	                        ruling.target == target
  3196	                    } else {
  3197	                        ruling.target == target_file
  3198	                    }
  3199	                    && ruling
  3200	                        .claim_requires
  3201	                        .iter()
  3202	                        .all(|phrase| prose.contains(phrase.as_str()))
  3203	                    && !ruling
  3204	                        .claim_excludes
  3205	                        .iter()
  3206	                        .any(|phrase| prose.contains(phrase.as_str()))
  3207	            })
  3208	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
  3209	        for ruling in &matched {
  3210	            *cleared.entry(ruling.id.clone()).or_insert(0u64) += 1;
  3211	        }
  3212	        if matched.is_empty() {
  3213	            unresolved += 1;
  3214	        }
  3215	    }
  3216	    for (id, count) in &cleared {
  3217	        anyhow::ensure!(
  3218	            *count <= 1,
  3219	            "ruling {id} cleared {count} separate findings in {record}; a ruling \
  3220	                 answers one claim, so phrases matching more than one are too \
  3221	                 broad to stand"
  3222	        );
  3223	    }
  3224	    Ok(unresolved)
  3225	}

  3229	/// The last assistant message in a codex rollout: what the provider actually
  3230	/// said, as its own transcript records it.

  3235	            continue;
  3236	        };

  3239	            || payload["type"] != "message"
  3240	            || payload["role"] != "assistant"
  3241	        {
  3242	            continue;
  3243	        }

  3245	            .as_array()?
  3246	            .iter()
  3247	            .filter_map(|part| part["text"].as_str())

  3254	/// A codex receipt: the session it names, the transcript it retained, and
  3255	/// that the answer beside the record is the one the transcript records the
  3256	/// provider giving.
  3257	fn verify_codex_receipt(record: &ReviewRecord, record_path: &Utf8Path) -> Result<()> {
  3258	    let receipt = &record.provider_receipt;
  3259	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3260	        !receipt.session_id.trim().is_empty() && !receipt.session_file.trim().is_empty(),
  3261	        "a codex receipt must name the session that answered"
  3262	    );
  3263	    require_hex_digest("review transcript_sha256", &receipt.transcript_sha256)?;
  3264	    let transcript = record_path.with_extension("session.jsonl");
  3265	    let bytes = fs::read(&transcript).with_context(|| {
  3266	        format!("{transcript}: the codex transcript must be retained beside its record")
  3267	    })?;
  3268	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3269	        bytes.len() as u64 == receipt.transcript_bytes,
  3270	        "codex transcript is {} bytes, receipt claims {}",
  3271	        bytes.len(),
  3272	        receipt.transcript_bytes
  3273	    );
  3274	    require_eq(
  3275	        "review transcript_sha256 (of the retained transcript)",
  3276	        &format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(&bytes)),
  3277	        &receipt.transcript_sha256,
  3278	    )?;
  3279	    // Blind pass 1 at `aeed70f9` (A09): the transcript's bytes were
  3280	    // authenticated and its IDENTITY was not — `session_id` and
  3281	    // `session_file` only had to be non-empty, so a record could name
  3282	    // one session and retain another's rollout. A rollout opens with
  3283	    // its own `session_meta`, and the receipt's id ends with the UUID
  3284	    // that record carries.
  3285	    let first = std::str::from_utf8(&bytes)
  3286	        .context("codex transcript is not UTF-8")?
  3287	        .lines()
  3288	        .next()
  3289	        .context("codex transcript is empty")?;
  3290	    let meta: serde_json::Value =
  3291	        serde_json::from_str(first).context("codex transcript's first record is not JSON")?;
  3292	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3293	        meta["type"] == "session_meta",
  3294	        "a codex rollout opens with session_meta; this one opens with {:?}",
  3295	        meta["type"]
  3296	    );
  3297	    let declared = meta["payload"]["session_id"]
  3298	        .as_str()
  3299	        .context("codex session_meta carries no session_id")?;
  3300	    // Codex names a rollout `<timestamp>-<uuid>` and its `session_meta`
  3301	    // carries the bare uuid, so the receipt's id either IS the declared
  3302	    // id or ends with it after a separator. Review of `bba803d4`: a
  3303	    // bare `ends_with` would also accept `xfixture` for `fixture`,
  3304	    // which is a different session.
  3305	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3306	        receipt.session_id == declared || receipt.session_id.ends_with(&format!("-{declared}")),
  3307	        "receipt names session {:?}, retained transcript is session {declared:?}",
  3308	        receipt.session_id
  3309	    );
  3310	    require_eq(
  3311	        "review provider_receipt session_file",
  3312	        &receipt.session_file,
  3313	        &format!("rollout-{}.jsonl", receipt.session_id),
  3314	    )?;
  3315	    // Blind pass 1 at `3720d179` (A09): the raw answer and the
  3316	    // transcript were each hashed and neither was checked against the
  3317	    // other, so a record could retain a real session and a different
  3318	    // answer — both digests true, the pair a fiction. The rollout's
  3319	    // last assistant message IS the answer the runner saved.
  3320	    let raw_path = record_path.with_extension("raw.txt");
  3321	    let raw = fs::read_to_string(&raw_path)
  3322	        .with_context(|| format!("{raw_path}: the raw answer must be retained"))?;
  3323	    let spoken = transcript_final_message(&bytes)
  3324	        .with_context(|| format!("{transcript}: the transcript carries no assistant message"))?;
  3325	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3326	        spoken.trim() == raw.trim(),
  3327	        "the retained answer is not the one the transcript records the provider giving"
  3328	    );
  3329	    Ok(())
  3330	}

  3332	fn verify_review_provider_receipt(record: &ReviewRecord, record_path: &Utf8Path) -> Result<()> {
  3333	    let receipt = &record.provider_receipt;
  3334	    require_eq(
  3335	        "review provider_receipt backend",
  3336	        &receipt.backend,
  3337	        &record.reviewer.backend,

  3340	        "codex" => verify_codex_receipt(record, record_path),
  3341	        "mimo-direct" => {
  3342	            anyhow::ensure!(
  3343	                !receipt.response_id.trim().is_empty(),
  3344	                "a mimo receipt must carry the provider's response id"
  3345	            );
  3346	            // Blind pass 1 at `3720d179` (A10): non-empty was the whole
  3347	            // check, so the provider could say it answered as anything and
  3348	            // the record's own `model_family` went uncompared. The receipt is
  3349	            // the provider's statement of who answered; if it does not name
  3350	            // the reviewer the record claims, one of the two is wrong.
  3351	            anyhow::ensure!(
  3352	                !receipt.provider_model.trim().is_empty(),
  3353	                "a mimo receipt must carry the model the provider says answered"
  3354	            );
  3355	            anyhow::ensure!(
  3356	                receipt
  3357	                    .provider_model
  3358	                    .contains(record.reviewer.model_family.as_str())
  3359	                    || record
  3360	                        .reviewer
  3361	                        .model_family
  3362	                        .contains(receipt.provider_model.as_str()),
  3363	                "the provider says {:?} answered and the record names {:?}",
  3364	                receipt.provider_model,
  3365	                record.reviewer.model_family
  3366	            );
  3367	            anyhow::ensure!(
  3368	                receipt.created > 0,
  3369	                "a mimo receipt must carry the provider's clock"
  3370	            );
  3371	            for key in ["prompt_tokens", "completion_tokens", "total_tokens"] {
  3372	                anyhow::ensure!(
  3373	                    receipt.usage.contains_key(key),
  3374	                    "a mimo receipt must carry the provider's {key}; a changed usage envelope \

  3376	                );
  3377	            }
  3378	            let billed = receipt
  3379	                .usage
  3380	                .get("total_tokens")
  3381	                .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_u64)
  3382	                .unwrap_or(0);
  3383	            anyhow::ensure!(
  3384	                billed > 0,
  3385	                "a mimo receipt must carry billed usage; {:?} bills nothing",
  3386	                receipt.usage
  3387	            );
  3388	            require_hex_digest("mimo provider content_sha256", &receipt.content_sha256)?;
  3389	            let raw_path = record_path.with_extension("raw.txt");
  3390	            let raw = fs::read(&raw_path)
  3391	                .with_context(|| format!("{raw_path}: the MiMo answer must be retained"))?;
  3392	            require_eq(
  3393	                "mimo provider content_sha256 (of the retained answer)",
  3394	                &format!("{:x}", Sha256::digest(&raw)),
  3395	                &receipt.content_sha256,
  3396	            )?;
  3397	            Ok(())
  3398	        }
  3399	        other => anyhow::bail!(
  3400	            "review backend {other:?} produced no provider receipt; ADR-0020 §6 independence \
  3401	             rests on evidence from outside this runner (F-49)"
  3402	        ),
  3403	    }

  3420	/// The commands a resolution receipt may claim, and the gate RUNS the one it
  3421	/// claims (A09/A10 at 9eca4f0).
  3422	///

  3424	/// `verification_exit_code: 0` was accepted without the command ever being
  3425	/// executed — the resolution asserted its own success. The command is drawn
  3426	/// from a closed registry rather than run as written: executing arbitrary text
  3427	/// out of an evidence file would hand whoever wrote the file this process.
  3428	const RESOLUTION_COMMANDS: [(&str, &[&str]); 4] = [
  3429	    ("just ci", &["just", "ci"]),
  3430	    ("just haq-inventory", &["just", "haq-inventory"]),
  3431	    ("just haq-canaries", &["just", "haq-canaries"]),
  3432	    (
  3433	        "cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features",
  3434	        &["cargo", "nextest", "run", "--workspace", "--all-features"],
  3435	    ),
  3436	];

  3438	/// The registry's commands are the project's own gates, run with the gate's
  3439	/// environment and no timeout: they are what CI runs, so a hang here is a hang
  3440	/// in CI, visible either way (review of `e490671`). The working directory is a
  3441	/// disposable worktree at the commit the receipt names, never the live tree.
  3442	fn verify_resolution_command_ran(
  3443	    root: &Utf8Path,
  3444	    who: &str,
  3445	    evidence_text: &str,
  3446	    commit: &str,
  3447	) -> Result<()> {
  3448	    let claimed = evidence_text
  3449	        .lines()
  3450	        .find_map(|line| line.trim_start().strip_prefix("verification_command:"))
  3451	        .map(str::trim)
  3452	        .unwrap_or_default();
  3453	    let argv = RESOLUTION_COMMANDS
  3454	        .iter()
  3455	        .find(|(name, _)| *name == claimed)
  3456	        .map(|(_, argv)| *argv)
  3457	        .with_context(|| {
  3458	            format!(
  3459	                "{who}: resolution claims verification command {claimed:?}, which is not one the \
  3460	                 gate can run; the registry is closed so a receipt cannot name a command that \
  3461	                 exists only in its own text"
  3462	            )
  3463	        })?;
  3464	    let (program, rest) = argv.split_first().context("registry command is empty")?;
  3465	    // Blind pass 1 at aecb2ec7 (A12): the command ran against the working
  3466	    // tree, so a receipt claiming a finding was resolved at some commit was
  3467	    // answered by whether the command passes at HEAD. Reachability was
  3468	    // checked and the commit then ignored. It runs in a disposable worktree
  3469	    // checked out at the claimed commit now, which is what the receipt says.
  3470	    let scratch = liminal_scratch::ScratchDir::new("haq-resolution-replay")?;
  3471	    let worktree = scratch.path().to_owned();
  3472	    let add = Command::new("git")
  3473	        .current_dir(root)
  3474	        .args(["worktree", "add", "--detach", "--quiet"])
  3475	        .arg(&worktree)
  3476	        .arg(commit)
  3477	        .output()?;
  3478	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3479	        add.status.success(),
  3480	        "{who}: resolution replay worktree add at {commit} failed: {}",
  3481	        String::from_utf8_lossy(&add.stderr).trim()
  3482	    );
  3483	    let mut guard = WorktreeGuard::new(root, &worktree);
  3484	    let status = Command::new(program)
  3485	        .current_dir(&worktree)
  3486	        .args(rest)
  3487	        .status()
  3488	        .with_context(|| format!("{who}: run resolution verification {claimed:?} at {commit}"))?;
  3489	    guard.remove()?;
  3490	    anyhow::ensure!(
  3491	        status.success(),
  3492	        "{who}: resolution claims {claimed:?} exited zero at {commit}; it exited {status}"
  3493	    );
  3494	    Ok(())
  3495	}

  2699	/// A reviewer cannot make its own "independent reproduction" true by setting
  2700	/// two booleans in one record. Every reproduced finding must have one matching
  2701	/// verified defect in the other isolated pass, with the same attack class,
  2702	/// exact source target, and identical falsification claim/observation. This

  2708	/// not write the same sentence, so a genuine independent reproduction was

  2710	/// blinding exists to prevent. The class and the coordinate already match by
  2711	/// the time this is asked; what is left to establish is that the two are about
  2712	/// the same thing, and shared vocabulary establishes it. Four significant
  2713	/// words in common is far more than coincidence at one coordinate and far less
  2714	/// than dictation.
  2715	fn reports_the_same_defect(

  2717	    right: &ReviewRecordAttempt,

  2719	    source_vocabulary: Option<&BTreeSet<String>>,

  2722	    // `crates`, `liminal`, `xtask` and `haq` were four shared words before

  2724	    // once as vocabulary. Words the coordinate already carries are struck out,
  2725	    // and so are the handful this campaign puts in every report.
  2726	    const UBIQUITOUS: [&str; 8] = [
  2727	        "verifier",
  2728	        "verify",
  2729	        "packet",
  2730	        "evidence",
  2731	        "check",
  2732	        "checks",
  2733	        "because",
  2734	        "committed",
  2735	    ];
  2736	    let coordinate: BTreeSet<String> = format!("{} {}", left.target, right.target)
  2737	        .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2738	        .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')
  2739	        .map(str::to_owned)
  2740	        .collect();
  2741	    let vocabulary = |attempt: &ReviewRecordAttempt| {
  2742	        format!("{} {}", attempt.attempt, attempt.observed_result)
  2743	            .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2744	            .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')
  2745	            .filter(|word| word.len() >= 4)
  2746	            .filter(|word| !coordinate.contains(*word))
  2747	            .filter(|word| !UBIQUITOUS.contains(word))
  2748	            .map(str::to_owned)
  2749	            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>()
  2750	    };

  2752	        .intersection(&vocabulary(right))
  2753	        .cloned()
  2754	        .collect();

  2756	        return false;
  2757	    }
  2758	    // Blind pass 1 at `2bba9071` (A09): four shared words is a count, and a
  2759	    // count is satisfied by four words this campaign puts in every report.
  2760	    // What makes two reports the same report is sharing something RARE — a
  2761	    // word that does not appear all over the rest of the record. Two such
  2762	    // words, measured against every attempt in both passes rather than
  2763	    // against a list someone maintains.
  2764	    let distinctive = shared
  2765	        .iter()
  2766	        .filter(|word| {

  2769	            // reports manufactured from four private nonce words while still
  2770	            // allowing independently worded descriptions of real code.

  2775	                .iter()
  2776	                .filter(|attempt| {
  2777	                    format!("{} {}", attempt.attempt, attempt.observed_result)
  2778	                        .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2779	                        .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')
  2780	                        .any(|token| token == word.as_str())
  2781	                })
  2782	                .count()
  2783	                <= 2
  2784	        })
  2785	        .count();

  2787	}

  2699	/// A reviewer cannot make its own "independent reproduction" true by setting
  2700	/// two booleans in one record. Every reproduced finding must have one matching
  2701	/// verified defect in the other isolated pass, with the same attack class,
  2702	/// exact source target, and identical falsification claim/observation. This

  2706	/// `0a0b4b4b` (A10): this required the `attempt` and `observed_result` strings

  2708	/// not write the same sentence, so a genuine independent reproduction was
  2709	/// rejected unless they coordinated wording — which is the one thing the
  2710	/// blinding exists to prevent. The class and the coordinate already match by
  2711	/// the time this is asked; what is left to establish is that the two are about
  2712	/// the same thing, and shared vocabulary establishes it. Four significant
  2713	/// words in common is far more than coincidence at one coordinate and far less
  2714	/// than dictation.
  2715	fn reports_the_same_defect(
  2716	    left: &ReviewRecordAttempt,
  2717	    right: &ReviewRecordAttempt,
  2718	    corpus: &[&ReviewRecordAttempt],
  2719	    source_vocabulary: Option<&BTreeSet<String>>,

  2722	    // `crates`, `liminal`, `xtask` and `haq` were four shared words before
  2723	    // either said anything — the coordinate matched twice, once as itself and
  2724	    // once as vocabulary. Words the coordinate already carries are struck out,
  2725	    // and so are the handful this campaign puts in every report.
  2726	    const UBIQUITOUS: [&str; 8] = [
  2727	        "verifier",
  2728	        "verify",
  2729	        "packet",
  2730	        "evidence",
  2731	        "check",
  2732	        "checks",
  2733	        "because",
  2734	        "committed",
  2735	    ];

  2737	        .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2738	        .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')
  2739	        .map(str::to_owned)
  2740	        .collect();
  2741	    let vocabulary = |attempt: &ReviewRecordAttempt| {
  2742	        format!("{} {}", attempt.attempt, attempt.observed_result)

  2744	            .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')

  2775	                .iter()
  2776	                .filter(|attempt| {
  2777	                    format!("{} {}", attempt.attempt, attempt.observed_result)
  2778	                        .to_ascii_lowercase()
  2779	                        .split(|ch: char| !ch.is_alphanumeric() && ch != '_')

  2781	                })
  2782	                .count()

 12577	            let mut skipping: Option<(usize, bool)> = None;
 12578	            let mut scanner = SourceScanner::default();
 12579	            for (index, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
 12580	                let trimmed = line.trim();
 12581	                let structural = scanner.structural(line);
 12582	                if let Some((depth, entered)) = skipping.as_mut() {
 12583	                    *depth += structural.matches('{').count();
 12584	                    let closes = structural.matches('}').count();
 12585	                    if *depth > 0 {
 12586	                        *entered = true;
 12587	                    }
 12588	                    *depth = depth.saturating_sub(closes);
 12589	                    if (*entered && *depth == 0) || (!*entered && trimmed.ends_with(';')) {
 12590	                        skipping = None;
 12591	                    }
 12592	                    continue;
 12593	                }
 12594	                if trimmed.replace(' ', "") == "#[cfg(test)]" {
 12595	                    skipping = Some((0, false));
 12596	                    continue;
 12597	                }
 12598	                if trimmed.starts_with("//") {
 12599	                    continue;
 12600	                }
 12601	                for token in CONCURRENCY_EXECUTION_PRIMITIVES {
 12602	                    if line.contains(token) {
 12603	                        scan.execution
 12604	                            .push(format!("{relative}:{}:{token}", index + 1));
 12605	                    }
 12606	                }
 12607	                for token in CONCURRENCY_SYNC_PRIMITIVES {
 12608	                    if line.contains(token) {
 12609	                        scan.sync.push(format!("{relative}:{}:{token}", index + 1));
 12610	                    }
 12611	                }
 12612	            }
 12613	        }
 12614	    }
 12615	    Ok(scan)
 12616	}

12100	fn require_unique<'a>(ids: impl Iterator<Item = &'a str>, label: &str) -> Result<()> {
 12101	    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
 12102	    for id in ids {
 12103	        if !seen.insert(id.to_owned()) {
 12104	            anyhow::bail!("duplicate {label} id {id}");
 12105	        }
 12106	    }
 12107	    Ok(())
 12108	}

 12111	    actual: impl Iterator<Item = &'a str>,
 12112	    expected: impl Iterator<Item = String>,
 12113	    label: &str,

 12115	    let actual = actual.map(ToOwned::to_owned).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
 12116	    let expected = expected.collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();

 12395	/// dependency asks the question again instead of answering it silently.

 12421	/// The external crates `manifest` depends on at run time, workspace members
 12422	/// excluded. Dev-dependencies are excluded too: the scan reads `src/` only,
 12423	/// which a dev-dependency cannot reach.
 12424	#[allow(clippy::items_after_statements)]
 12425	fn runtime_external_dependencies(manifest: &Utf8Path) -> Result<BTreeSet<String>> {
 12426	    let text = fs::read_to_string(manifest).with_context(|| format!("read {manifest}"))?;
 12427	    let mut out = BTreeSet::new();
 12428	    let value: toml::Value = toml::from_str(&text).with_context(|| format!("parse {manifest}"))?;
 12429	    fn collect(value: &toml::Value, path: &mut Vec<String>, out: &mut BTreeSet<String>) {
 12430	        let toml::Value::Table(table) = value else {
 12431	            return;
 12432	        };
 12433	        let is_runtime = path.last().is_some_and(|part| part == "dependencies")
 12434	            && !path
 12435	                .iter()
 12436	                .any(|part| part == "dev-dependencies" || part == "build-dependencies");
 12437	        if is_runtime {
 12438	            for (key, spec) in table {
 12439	                // Cargo's `package = "real-name"` is authoritative when the
 12440	                // dependency key is an alias. Checking only the key lets a
 12441	                // spawn-capable crate hide behind an allowed alias (A06).
 12442	                let package = spec
 12443	                    .as_table()
 12444	                    .and_then(|spec| spec.get("package"))
 12445	                    .and_then(toml::Value::as_str)
 12446	                    .unwrap_or(key);
 12447	                if !package.is_empty() && !package.starts_with("liminal") {
 12448	                    out.insert(package.to_owned());
 12449	                }
 12450	            }
 12451	        }
 12452	        for (key, child) in table {
 12453	            path.push(key.clone());
 12454	            collect(child, path, out);
 12455	            path.pop();
 12456	        }
 12457	    }
 12458	    collect(&value, &mut Vec::new(), &mut out);
 12459	    Ok(out)
 12460	}

 12479	    "::scope",

 12495	/// Scan the implementation crates' non-test sources for concurrency
 12496	/// primitives. A file's trailing `#[cfg(test)]` module is skipped; comment
 12497	/// lines are skipped. Deterministic order: crates, files and lines sorted.
 12498	fn scan_concurrency_primitives(root: &Utf8Path) -> Result<ConcurrencyScan> {
 12499	    // DG17.5: inspect the resolved workspace, not dependency keys (which alias).
 12500	    // Source-only test fixtures have no workspace manifest and admit no vstd.
 12501	    let vstd_admitted = root.join("Cargo.toml").is_file() && crate::vstd_admission::admitted(root)?;

 12505	fn concurrency_dependency_allowed(dependency: &str, vstd_admitted: bool) -> bool {
 12506	    CONCURRENCY_SCAN_ALLOWED_DEPENDENCIES.contains(&dependency)
 12507	        || (vstd_admitted && dependency == "vstd")

 12510	fn scan_concurrency_sources(root: &Utf8Path, vstd_admitted: bool) -> Result<ConcurrencyScan> {
 12511	    fn walk(dir: &Utf8Path, out: &mut Vec<Utf8PathBuf>) -> Result<()> {
 12512	        let mut entries = fs::read_dir(dir.as_std_path())
 12513	            .with_context(|| format!("read {dir}"))?
 12514	            .map(|entry| entry.map(|e| e.path()))
 12515	            .collect::<std::io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
 12516	        entries.sort();
 12517	        for path in entries {
 12518	            let path = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(path)
 12519	                .map_err(|p| anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path {}", p.display()))?;
 12520	            if path.is_dir() {
 12521	                walk(&path, out)?;
 12522	            } else if path.extension() == Some("rs") {
 12523	                out.push(path);
 12524	            }
 12525	        }
 12526	        Ok(())
 12527	    }
 12528	    let mut scan = ConcurrencyScan {
 12529	        execution: Vec::new(),
 12530	        sync: Vec::new(),
 12531	    };
 12532	    let crates_dir = root.join("crates");
 12533	    let mut crate_dirs = fs::read_dir(crates_dir.as_std_path())
 12534	        .with_context(|| format!("read {crates_dir}"))?
 12535	        .map(|entry| entry.map(|e| e.path()))
 12536	        .collect::<std::io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
 12537	    crate_dirs.sort();
 12538	    for member in crate_dirs {
 12539	        let member_dir = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(member)
 12540	            .map_err(|p| anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path {}", p.display()))?;
 12541	        let Some(name) = member_dir.file_name() else {
 12542	            continue;
 12543	        };
 12544	        if CONCURRENCY_SCAN_EXCLUDED_CRATES.contains(&name) || !member_dir.join("src").is_dir() {
 12545	            continue;
 12546	        }
 12547	        let manifest = member_dir.join("Cargo.toml");
 12548	        if manifest.is_file() {
 12549	            let external = runtime_external_dependencies(&manifest)?;
 12550	            let unknown = external
 12551	                .iter()
 12552	                .filter(|dep| !concurrency_dependency_allowed(dep, vstd_admitted))
 12553	                .cloned()
 12554	                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 12555	            anyhow::ensure!(
 12556	                unknown.is_empty(),
 12557	                "{name} depends on {unknown:?}, outside the closed list the \
 12558	                 concurrency scan reasons about; a dependency may export a \
 12559	                 macro that spawns, which a lexical scan cannot see. Decide, \
 12560	                 then widen CONCURRENCY_SCAN_ALLOWED_DEPENDENCIES"
 12561	            );
 12562	        }
 12563	        let mut files = Vec::new();
 12564	        walk(&member_dir.join("src"), &mut files)?;
 12565	        for file in files {
 12566	            let text = fs::read_to_string(&file).with_context(|| format!("read {file}"))?;
 12567	            let relative = file.strip_prefix(root).unwrap_or(&file);
 12568	            // Blind pass 1 at 612cbcc (A06): this used to stop at the first
 12569	            // `#[cfg(test)]` line, so production code after an earlier test
 12570	            // module escaped the scan. The attributed item is skipped as a
 12571	            // block (brace depth) or, for a brace-less item, through its `;`,
 12572	            // and scanning resumes after it. F-56: braces used to be
 12573	            // counted textually, strings and comments included, so an
 12574	            // unbalanced brace inside a test module could end the skip late
 12575	            // and hide a production spawn. Only structural braces count now,
 12576	            // the same scanner the mutant anchor screen uses.
 12577	            let mut skipping: Option<(usize, bool)> = None;
 12578	            let mut scanner = SourceScanner::default();
 12579	            for (index, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
 12580	                let trimmed = line.trim();
 12581	                let structural = scanner.structural(line);
 12582	                if let Some((depth, entered)) = skipping.as_mut() {
 12583	                    *depth += structural.matches('{').count();
 12584	                    let closes = structural.matches('}').count();
 12585	                    if *depth > 0 {
 12586	                        *entered = true;
 12587	                    }
 12588	                    *depth = depth.saturating_sub(closes);
 12589	                    if (*entered && *depth == 0) || (!*entered && trimmed.ends_with(';')) {
 12590	                        skipping = None;
 12591	                    }
 12592	                    continue;
 12593	                }
 12594	                if trimmed.replace(' ', "") == "#[cfg(test)]" {
 12595	                    skipping = Some((0, false));
 12596	                    continue;
 12597	                }
 12598	                if trimmed.starts_with("//") {
 12599	                    continue;
 12600	                }
 12601	                for token in CONCURRENCY_EXECUTION_PRIMITIVES {
 12602	                    if line.contains(token) {
 12603	                        scan.execution
 12604	                            .push(format!("{relative}:{}:{token}", index + 1));
 12605	                    }
 12606	                }
 12607	                for token in CONCURRENCY_SYNC_PRIMITIVES {
 12608	                    if line.contains(token) {
 12609	                        scan.sync.push(format!("{relative}:{}:{token}", index + 1));
 12610	                    }
 12611	                }
 12612	            }
 12613	        }
 12614	    }
 12615	    Ok(scan)
 12616	}

 12421	/// The external crates `manifest` depends on at run time, workspace members

 12423	/// which a dev-dependency cannot reach.
 12424	#[allow(clippy::items_after_statements)]
 12425	fn runtime_external_dependencies(manifest: &Utf8Path) -> Result<BTreeSet<String>> {
 12426	    let text = fs::read_to_string(manifest).with_context(|| format!("read {manifest}"))?;
 12427	    let mut out = BTreeSet::new();
 12428	    let value: toml::Value = toml::from_str(&text).with_context(|| format!("parse {manifest}"))?;
 12429	    fn collect(value: &toml::Value, path: &mut Vec<String>, out: &mut BTreeSet<String>) {
 12430	        let toml::Value::Table(table) = value else {
 12431	            return;
 12432	        };
 12433	        let is_runtime = path.last().is_some_and(|part| part == "dependencies")
 12434	            && !path
 12435	                .iter()
 12436	                .any(|part| part == "dev-dependencies" || part == "build-dependencies");
 12437	        if is_runtime {
 12438	            for (key, spec) in table {
 12439	                // Cargo's `package = "real-name"` is authoritative when the
 12440	                // dependency key is an alias. Checking only the key lets a
 12441	                // spawn-capable crate hide behind an allowed alias (A06).
 12442	                let package = spec
 12443	                    .as_table()
 12444	                    .and_then(|spec| spec.get("package"))
 12445	                    .and_then(toml::Value::as_str)
 12446	                    .unwrap_or(key);
 12447	                if !package.is_empty() && !package.starts_with("liminal") {
 12448	                    out.insert(package.to_owned());
 12449	                }
 12450	            }
 12451	        }
 12452	        for (key, child) in table {
 12453	            path.push(key.clone());
 12454	            collect(child, path, out);
 12455	            path.pop();
 12456	        }
 12457	    }
 12458	    collect(&value, &mut Vec::new(), &mut out);
 12459	    Ok(out)
 12460	}
