 12510	fn scan_concurrency_sources(root: &Utf8Path, vstd_admitted: bool) -> Result<ConcurrencyScan> {
 12511	    fn walk(dir: &Utf8Path, out: &mut Vec<Utf8PathBuf>) -> Result<()> {
 12512	        let mut entries = fs::read_dir(dir.as_std_path())
 12513	            .with_context(|| format!("read {dir}"))?
 12514	            .map(|entry| entry.map(|e| e.path()))
 12515	            .collect::<std::io::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
 12516	        entries.sort();
 12517	        for path in entries {
 12518	            let path = Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(path)
 12519	                .map_err(|p| anyhow::anyhow!("non-UTF-8 path {}", p.display()))?;
 12520	            if path.is_dir() {
 12521	                walk(&path, out)?;
 12522	            } else if path.extension() == Some("rs") {
 12523	                out.push(path);
 12524	            }
 12525	        }
 12526	        Ok(())
 12527	    }
 12528	    let mut scan = ConcurrencyScan {
 12529	        execution: Vec::new(),
 12530	        sync: Vec::new(),
 12531	    };
 12532	    let crates_dir = root.join("crates");
 12533	    let mut crate_dirs = fs::read_dir(crates_dir.as_std_path())
 12534	        .with_context(|| format!("read {crates_dir}"))?
 12535	        .map(|entry| entry.map(|e| e.path()))
 12536	        .collect::<std::io::Result<Vec<_>>>…207 tokens truncated… 12553	                .cloned()
 12554	                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 12555	            anyhow::ensure!(
 12556	                unknown.is_empty(),
 12557	                "{name} depends on {unknown:?}, outside the closed list the \
 12558	                 concurrency scan reasons about; a dependency may export a \
 12559	                 macro that spawns, which a lexical scan cannot see. Decide, \
 12560	                 then widen CONCURRENCY_SCAN_ALLOWED_DEPENDENCIES"
 12561	            );
 12562	        }
 12563	        let mut files = Vec::new();
 12564	        walk(&member_dir.join("src"), &mut files)?;
 12565	        for file in files {
 12566	            let text = fs::read_to_string(&file).with_context(|| format!("read {file}"))?;
 12567	            let relative = file.strip_prefix(root).unwrap_or(&file);
 12568	            // Blind pass 1 at 612cbcc (A06): this used to stop at the first
 12569	            // `#[cfg(test)]` line, so production code after an earlier test
 12570	            // module escaped the scan. The attributed item is skipped as a
 12571	            // block (brace depth) or, for a brace-less item, through its `;`,
 12572	            // and scanning resumes after it. F-56: braces used to be
 12573	            // counted textually, strings and comments included, so an
 12574	            // unbalanced brace inside a test module could end the skip late
 12575	            // and hide a production spawn. Only structural braces count now,
 12576	            // the same scanner the mutant anchor screen uses.
 12577	            let mut skipping: Option<(usize, bool)> = None;
 12578	            let mut scanner = SourceScanner::default();
 12579	            for (index, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
 12580	                let trimmed = line.trim();
 12581	                let structural = scanner.structural(line);
 12582	                if let Some((depth, entered)) = skipping.as_mut() {
 12583	                    *depth += structural.matches('{').count();
 12584	                    let closes = structural.matches('}').count();
 12585	                    if *depth > 0 {
 12586	                        *entered = true;
 12587	                    }
 12588	                    *depth = depth.saturating_sub(closes);
 12589	                    if (*entered && *depth == 0) || (!*entered && trimmed.ends_with(';')) {
 12590	                        skipping = None;
 12591	                    }
 12592	                    continue;
 12593	                }
 12594	                if trimmed.replace(' ', "") == "#[cfg(test)]" {
 12595	                    skipping = Some((0, false));
 12596	                    continue;
 12597	                }
 12598	                if trimmed.starts_with("//") {
 12599	                    continue;
 12600	                }
 12601	                for token in CONCURRENCY_EXECUTION_PRIMITIVES {
 12602	                    if line.contains(token) {
 12603	                        scan.execution
 12604	                            .push(format!("{relative}:{}:{token}", index + 1));
 12605	                    }
 12606	                }
 12607	                for token in CONCURRENCY_SYNC_PRIMITIVES {
 12608	                    if line.contains(token) {
 12609	                        scan.sync.push(format!("{relative}:{}:{token}", index + 1));
 12610	                    }
 12611	                }
 12612	            }
 12613	        }
 12614	    }
 12615	    Ok(scan)
 12616	}

  1357	fn verify_generated_rows(
  1358	    root: &Utf8Path,
  1359	    declared: &[Generated],
  1360	    recorded: &[GeneratedEvidence],
  1361	) -> Result<()> {
  1362	    let mut by_family = BTreeMap::new();
  1363	    for row in recorded {
  1364	        if by_family.insert(row.family.as_str(), row).is_some() {
  1365	            anyhow::bail!("generated evidence repeats family {:?}", row.family);
  1366	        }
  1367	    }
  1368	    for family in declared {
  1369	        if family.result != "pass" {
  1370	            continue;
  1371	        }
  1372	        let evidence = by_family.get(family.family.as_str()).with_context(|| {
  1373	            format!(
  1374	                "{} claims pass but the committed generated evidence has no such family",
  1375	                family.family
  1376	            )
  1377	        })?;
  1378	        // The hash covers the family's whole accept/discard stream and cannot
  1379	        // be recomputed here without rerunning 100,000 cases. It is bound
  1380	        // instead to the digest the RUN recorded, which is the strongest check
  1381	        // available at verification time: the packet may no longer cite a
  1382	        // number no run produced. Determinism of that digest is pinned
  1383	        // separately by `generated_evidence_is_byte_identical_across_runs`, so
  1384	        // editing the committed artifact to match a doctored packet is
  1385	        // detectable by rerunning the generator.
  1386	        let claimed = family
  1387	            .evidence_hash
  1388	            .as_deref()
  1389	            .context("inventory layer requires a hash before `pass`")?;
  1390	        if !claimed.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&evidence.evidence_hash) {
  1391	            anyhow::bail!(
  1392	                "{}: packet claims evidence hash {claimed} but the committed run recorded {}",
  1393	                family.family,
  1394	                evidence.evidence_hash
  1395	            );
  1396	        }
  1397	        for (label, packet_value, evidence_value) in [
  1398	            ("accepted", family.accepted, evidence.accepted),
  1399	            ("attempts", family.attempts, evidence.attempts),
  1400	            ("discards", family.discards, evidence.discards),
  1401	            ("negatives", family.negatives, evidence.negatives),
  1402	        ] {
  1403	            if packet_value != evidence_value {
  1404	                anyhow::bail!(
  1405	                    "{}: packet declares {packet_value} {label} but the committed run recorded {evidence_value}",
  1406	                    family.family
  1407	                );
  1408	            }
  1409	        }
  1410	        if family.seed != Some(evidence.seed) {
  1411	            anyhow::bail!(
  1412	                "{}: packet declares seed {:?} but the committed run used {}",
  1413	                family.family,
  1414	                family.seed,
  1415	                evidence.seed
  1416	            );
  1417	        }
  1418	        verify_generated_contract(root, family, evidence)?;
  1419	    }
  1420	    Ok(())
  1421	}

  2173	            .find(|token| token.starts_with("{#") && token.ends_with('}'))

  2175	                || {
  2176	                    let key = format!("anon:{anonymous}");
  2177	                    anonymous += 1;
  2178	                    key
  2179	                },
  2180	                str::to_owned,
  2181	            );
  2182	        let tokens = block
  2183	            .split_whitespace()
  2184	            .filter(|token| !token.starts_with("{#") || !token.ends_with('}'))
  2185	            .map(str::to_owned)

  2188	        // order can falsify this ordering oracle; marker order is checked above.
  2189	        if !tokens.is_empty() {

  2177	                    anonymous += 1;
  2178	                    key
  2179	                },
  2180	                str::to_owned,
  2181	            );

  2183	            .split_whitespace()
  2184	            .filter(|token| !token.starts_with("{#") || !token.ends_with('}'))
  2185	            .map(str::to_owned)

  2167	fn ordered_block_contents(text: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>> {
  2168	    let mut anonymous = 0usize;
  2169	    let mut blocks = BTreeMap::new();
  2170	    for block in text.split("\n\n") {
  2171	        let marker = block
  2172	            .split_whitespace()
  2173	            .find(|token| token.starts_with("{#") && token.ends_with('}'))
  2174	            .map_or_else(
  2175	                || {
  2176	                    let key = format!("anon:{anonymous}");
  2177	                    anonymous += 1;
  2178	                    key
  2179	                },
  2180	                str::to_owned,
  2181	            );
  2182	        let tokens = block
  2183	            .split_whitespace()
  2184	            .filter(|token| !token.starts_with("{#") || !token.ends_with('}'))
  2185	            .map(str::to_owned)
  2186	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();

  2188	        // order can falsify this ordering oracle; marker order is checked above.
  2189	        if !tokens.is_empty() {
  2190	            blocks.insert(marker, tokens);
  2191	        }

  2194	}
